**22:02 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** Hey Plebs!
    
    David here, core contributor to CGP and co-founder of Afterparty AI, the leading platform for creators to fully own, control, and monetize their AI personas. We've developed some of the most realistic and high-quality AI models tailored for individuals. The primary challenge in expanding conversational AI to allow everyone to have their own personalized AI—both for themselves and for their loved ones—lies in obtaining high-quality annotated conversational data.
    
    The Conversation Genome Project (CGP) aims to address the fundamental challenge in developing natural and engaging conversational AI: the lack of personalization across cultural, interest-level, demographic, and psychographic differences. The CGP provides an open-source dataset indexed and tagged across billions of multivariate data points, enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to bring individual context to every interaction. 
    
    The digital commodity of the subnet is Structured Data. Starting with conversation data, we are building out the infrastructure for a decentralized Scale AI where validators can sell access to their bandwidth for any arbitrary data processing needs, all while preserving the privacy of the data with the subnet’s unique design and use of Conversation Windows (more about that here: https://conversations.xyz/p/cgp_overview)

**18:20 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** CGP is democratizing access to the key ingredient that drives LLM performance today: structured data. This is the digital community of our subnet.
    ​
    I wrote a blog post outlining what CGP brings to Bittensor and the broader AI community here: https://conversations.xyz/p/cgpblog4_annotateddatasets
    ​
    By tagging and indexing all the world's conversations, AI will be able to understand and interact in more human-like ways, making conversations with AI as natural as talking to a friend.
    ​
    The CGP dataset has immediate implications for the Bittensor community. Each conversation automatically generates multiple persona profiles, system prompts for those personas. Currently, Subnet 1 uses limited personas, ~1,000 combinations, opening up potential attack vectors.  The CGP will continuously generate millions of persona profiles, providing robustness and defense against potential miner attacks on SN 1.
    ​
    Creating personas from conversation data is something we will enable shortly for everyone. Users will be able to create personas of themselves, loved ones, or anyone they desire with just some conversation data they can process through validators on SN33. They can then interact with that persona via AI applications built exclusively on Bittensor infrastructure with our subnet and the subnet 18 API.
    ​
    We are building the infrastructure for personalized AIs for everyone 🌐
    (embed) Conversation Genome Project | Blog 4

**19:42 Rushing_to_freedom:** In this post you wrote: "Miners analyze conversation windows using Large Language Models (LLM) with different window sizes and refine participant profiles". Please tell us in a little more detail how this will happen?
**20:39 jvl:** Hey There! The basic flow of the subnet is as follows: 
    
    1. Validators get a full conversation from our API endpoint & Tag the full conversation (establishing ground truth)
    
    2. Validators then batch the full conversation into "windows" and send out to miners. The window size is currently based on the context window of GPT3.5 which is roughly 8000 tokens, however we will shortly be moving to a more dynamic window sizing algo that will accommodate whatever LLM you are using to tag the window.
    
    3. Miners Receive this window and provide tags for that window. Currently they are mining tags for the window overall, however in the next week or two we will be pushing an update after which miners will mine for specific tag types. For example "Personality of speaker A", "Personality of Speaker B","Hobbies of Speaker B", "Topics", "tone", etc. 
    
    4. Miners send their tags to the Validator, where tags are scored for their proximity to the semantic neighborhood of the "ground truth" tags that the validator generated on the full conversation in step 1.
    
    5. Miner Final Score is calculated from the Following components: Mean Top 3 Unique Tag Scores, mean of all tag scores (includes unique and non-unique), median tag score (includes unique and non-unique), max tag score. Scores are penalized if they do not contain 3 or more unique tags, if they don't share at least 1 tag with the ground truth, or if they don't have at least 2 tags overall.

**21:46 jvl:** Great Question! This work could (and traditionally is/was) done by people in the broader AI ecosystem. Our Subnet's goal is to automate this process to enable depthful data processing and tagging at scale and at a fraction of the cost. Miners in this subnet are bittensor users running the miner code in our repo (see first pinned post), tagging the dialogue data using LLMs. 
    
    You can think of this subnet as an automated and decentralized Scale AI - which processes and tags data for LLM training using a network of human labor across the globe. We, on the other hand, use the power of LLMs to carry out this work and therefore do not offer a web interface for human tagging.

**21:39 jvl:** Hey There! Thank you for your interest in our subnet and I’m here to help provide some guidance on how to optimize your mining set-up. You’re correct in your assumption that the primary area for mining optimization is in the scoring of your tags. 
    
    We’ve just pushed an update that allows you to set a file path to write the conversation windows and tags you mined to a local file for analysis. To enable this feature, please pull the latest main branch, copy and uncomment the line `export SCORING_DEBUG_LOG=./scoring_debug.log` to your .env file, and restart your miner. Then, your windows and tags will be written to the file `scoring_debug.log.`
    
    Please also familiarize yourself with the validator scoring algorithm in `conversationgenome/validator/evaluator.py` as this will help you understand how the tags generated by your miner are scored. The general explanation: for each tag your miner generates, the validator performs a distance calculation between the embedding of that tag and the semantic neighborhood of the “ground truth” tags that the validator generates from the full conversation. These individual tag scores inform a number of metrics used to calculate the final score. Please also see our blog postings on https://conversations.xyz for more information on this.
    
    Once you get a feel for how the mining process and rewards system works, we believe the primary areas for iteration and improvement are: 
    
    **LLM Model Selection.** Currently, you can use any of the public OpenAI LLMs out-of-the-box to generate your tags, and the default value is GPT-3.5. As you may know, OpenAI just released a large update this week, so we are eager to see miners experimenting with GPT-4o and other next-gen models. Shortly we will have an update out that enables tag harvesting with groq, Anthropic, and Local LLM importing. 
    
    **Fine-tuning Local Models. **It is likely that there is the ability to fine-tune an LLM to perform this task exceptionally well, which would increase your ability to harvest meaningful tags and thusly increase your scores.
    
    **Embedding Model Selection.** As you pointed out, the default embeddings model is the `text-embedding-ada-002` model from OpenAI, however we encourage experimentation with different embeddings models. Please keep in mind this area of improvement requires familiarity with vector embeddings and compatibility between these models.
    
    **System Prompt Tuning**. There is currently a default System Prompt that gets sent to the LLM with each conversation window, however this system prompt could/should be iterated on for the best possible response.
    
    Please let me know if you have any further questions here. Happy mining!

**21:35 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** ## SN3️⃣ 3️⃣ 🌐  has been live for 1 ½ weeks! 
    We wanted to provide an update and share our near-term roadmap. Thank you all for being early supporters of what we are building. As always, if you have any feedback or suggestions, please reach out to me or <@538101635478454272>. Since launch, we have released 3 updates and plan to continue building and pushing code quickly. 
     
    ## The newest version CGP 1.3.3 enables:
    * Mining and Validating with Groq and Anthropic models
    * Tag Reports for miners to optimize performance
    * Improved error trapping/reporting for Validators
     
    # SN33 Roadmap
    ## Personas API - launching next week
    * Thousands of personas created from the SN33 dataset, which can be used for character/roleplaying chat experiences, in-game character assets, e-commerce chatbots, and more. Available via API and Firebase.
    * The Personas API will ultimately enable any validator to sell access to users to process text or audio data through the CGP and develop their own Personas. Some use cases:
     * Persona of a loved one (grandfather, mother, etc.) 
     * Persona of a long lost friend or ex you have had text conversations with and want to get answers from. 
    * Enterprise Personas API 
     * This will also enable enterprise customers to process annotated data and create chatbots for their businesses (think restaurants, small businesses) and e-commerce sites.
    ## Largest Annotated Conversational Dataset(!)
    * We have already processed over 10 million lines of data, which exceeds the largest dataset of its kind (PersonalDialog). We will publish the dataset to Huggingface shortly and continually update it.
    * This is very valuable for the open-source community to use for fine-tuning conversational AI models. We are working with several AI researchers on this dataset and will publish the results of those models.
    ## Dynamic RAG
    * The CGP’s vector database will ultimately allow an LLM to dynamically change its personality as it speaks to a user and understands their personality, mood, and interests. 
    ## Other improvements coming to SN33:
    * Launch local model support 
    * Expand tagging categories to include personality traits, opinions, interests, topics, and more.
    * Optimize the data processing pipeline for performance
    * Continuously expanding and refining the dataset based on community feedback and evolving conversational AI research needs
    * Partnering with applications to power finetuned persona AIs utilizing the dataset

**08:06 Wouter:** Hi <@538101635478454272> ,
    
    I've been working on refining my miner code and wanted to discuss the current penalty system for tag mismatches. I understand the intent behind ensuring tag accuracy, but the 0.75 multiplier for not having an identical string/tag as the validator feels quite limiting.
    
    Could we consider adjusting this penalty to a range of 0.85 to 0.95? This change might encourage miners to develop tags that better capture the true content of the conversation windows, without feeling overly constrained by the baseline tags from the validators. I believe this could enhance the overall tagging quality.
    
    Thanks for considering this!
**17:58 jvl:** Hey <@310125915667431435> ! Thanks so much for the feedback - we are always looking for input on how to improve the reward mechanism.
    
    Currently, we are in the process of designing a new tagging framework, and an improved scoring algorithm to go with it. The new system will incentivize detailed and segmented tagging for different facets of the conversation, such as personality of Speaker A/B/C, Hobbies of Speaker A/B/C, tone and themes of conversation, etc etc. With this new approach to tagging we will have a revamped scoring system and set of penalties as well. We will definitely keep your feedback in mind when assigning weights and pentalties.
    
    That being said, in our testing, we found that the best sets of tags always shared at least one tag with the ground truth, and it was rare to generate a set that didn't share at least one. Based on this, we gathered that tag sets that didn't share any tags with the ground truth were most likely inaccurate, which is how we landed on this penalty.  Are you finding that you're facing this penalty often? If you're open to it, feel free to shoot me a PM with any data you have gathered on this, I would love to understand why that might be happening. Thanks again!

    Today, we launched the **Personas API**, introducing thousands of life-like personas that bring applications to life with AI personalized to business needs, all derived from mined conversations on CGP.

    We are also fine-tuning some models based on the full corpus of CGP data for prominent creators in the Bittensor ecosystem. Excited to share those very soon!
    
    ## Subnet Upgrades
    Miners are continue to optimize and improve their tagging of the conversational data. Inspired by SN12 and SN19, we are developing “dynamic miner context windows” that will allow miners to earn exponential rewards on a single UID.

    * Ensured consistent response parsing.

**17:27 Kat | Fren One:** For subtensor, the requirements from the GitHub are:
    
    ```    Subtensor needs access to the public internet
        Subtensor runs on ipv4
        Subtensor listens on the following ports:
            9944 - Websocket. This port is used by bittensor. It only accepts connections from localhost. Make sure this port is firewalled off from the public domain.
            9933 - RPC. This port is opened, but not used.
            30333 - p2p socket. This port accepts connections from other subtensor nodes. Make sure your firewall(s) allow incoming traffic to this port.
        It is assumed your default outgoing traffic policy is ACCEPT. If not, make sure outbound traffic to port 30333 is allowed.```
    
    Note that since you're on runpod, I beleive you're going to have to do some asymmetric port mapping.  Runpod's docs on that are here: https://docs.runpod.io/pods/configuration/expose-ports

**17:36 Kat | Fren One:** This is printed after your validator scores a step, which is its scoring of window tags generated by 3 miners.  It feeds into the moving average of your validator's weights for those miners as it works through the entire conversation (broken up into windows).  When it's time (roughly every 30 minutes, as I understand it) to set weights, it uses this information to do so, and the process resets.
**17:41 jvl:** this chart is measuring based on step, not time. meaning that while validator 66 might be at step 250k, what is step 250k for them might be step 100k for another validator that restarted their run more recently.
**17:45 jvl:** so this analysis is averaging your scores across all runs, not just your most recent performance. Your current incentive takes into account score history but also heavily weights recent historical performance. So while miner_eval is a good tool for analyzing your tag scoring performance, it isn't a perfect measure of how close to dereg you are at any given moment. The performance spread across miners is small in this subnet, which is a challenge we are working on presently. For now, the best explanation i have is that your recent performance is what's leading decreasing your relative incentive score, but we will continue to look into this.
**17:46 jvl:** Thank you for this feedback. We've gotten this note before and have several updates that we are considering to help minimize the effect of the both_tags penalty. I agree, 25% is a steep penalty, and this portion of the rewards mechanism could be optimized further.

    I would like to propose a revision to the current reward system, as there appear to be some significant issues with its current implementation. Below, I outline several key areas where improvements are necessary to ensure a fair and effective system.
    
    Verification Process: The current verification process does not adequately confirm whether a vector is genuinely associated with the intended tag. Consequently, miners can exploit this by simply finding vectors with high cosine similarity. For example, the ``np.mean`` of the vector of tags typically yields a score of not less than 0.96. There are other methods as well to achieve high cosine similarity without genuine correlation. I will provide the example score got by unfair way.
    
    Scoring Function: The ``update_score`` function relies on ``rank_scores``, where ``rank_score`` is essentially ``adjusted_score``. This means that penalties, apart from the ``tag_num penalty``, are not factored into the weight settings. As a result, the ``final_score`` serves no substantial purpose beyond being a decorative element.
    
    Validator Efficiency: If the validator employs the OpenAI API and opts for the cost-effective GPT-3.5-turbo model, miners can bypass the need to accurately identify tags. Given that typical conversations encompass no more than a few dozen topics, miners can prepare standard responses to achieve high scores without incurring API costs. Common topic tags include relationships, music, sports, science, love, community, health, wealth, age, adults, memories, entertainment, and others.
    
    In light of these points, I strongly recommend that the foundational code and reward system of the subnet be revised. Such changes are crucial to creating a level playing field and ensuring the integrity of the product.

    #export LLM_TYPE=openai
    #export LLM_TYPE=groq
    export LLM_TYPE=anthropic```
    
    And the Anthropic section is filled out correctly:```
    # ____________ ANTHROPIC Configuration: ________________
    # *** Below Fields Required if you chose LLM_TYPE=anthropic -- https://claude.ai/ ***
    export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
    
    # Enter a model below. See all options (use "Latest 1P API model name"): https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/models#model-names
    export ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-3-sonnet-20240229
    ```
    (With the appropriate model selected and API key provided)

**17:41 jvl:** **Subnet Update** <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    It has come to our attention recently that there are a number of miners scoring abnormally high on their tag sets on nearly every step (0.99+ average scores across thousands of steps).
    
    Our database leverages an endless stream of transcribed podcasts and youtube clips across the entire internet to feed to miners for tagging.
    
    In our subnet code, we take many steps to prevent lookup attacks. For example, conversation GUIDs are temporary values uniquely mapped across all conversation windows, to prevent key consistency and reduce lookup potential. Additionally, we structured the database pipeline to serve large batches of new conversations daily, keeping data fresh.
    
    Despite taking these steps, it appears that sometime in June our data sources became restricted, and the number of new conversations being served to validators decreased.
    
    As of today, we have refactored our database pipeline, and new conversations are flowing. Daily, there will be upwards of 300000 new lines of dialogue being served to miners and validators. In addition to the data expansion, we have introduced a new internal protocol where we will be adding new transcript sources every week, expanding our working dataset exponentially. Each source feeds in podcasts, news sources, youtube videos, and other types of data that is scraped daily for new episodes/content. This will ensure an ever-evolving, diverse firehose of data that will make lookup attacks virtually impossible.
    
    This change has occurred in the CGP Conversation store, and therefore requires no update to miners or validators. Honest miners, you should see no change to your scores, however we expect your incentive will likely begin to increase due to normalization of dishonest miner scores. We will be actively monitoring incentive levels and miner scores over the next few days to ensure that the problem has been solved.
    
    Thank you to our active community members <@806874851088138240>  and <@410552130680651798>  for bringing this to our attention. If anyone has questions, please feel free to reach out any time.

This unfortunately seems a problem with the practice of weight copying and not necessarily anything to do with the subnet, but we will continue to look into this

**18:31 jvl:** **New Release Live - CGP 1.91.14**
    
    <@&1237015679023059017> We just pushed out a new release to the main branch with the following updates:
    
    * Validator-Side Tag Cleaning & Embeddings
     * All embeddings used to generate scores will be generated by the validator immediately prior to scoring. This prevents a potential gamification by passing mismatching tags and vectors.
     * Validator and Miner Tags will also be cleaned prior to going through scoring algo to ensure matching formatting, limiting both unfair penalties and potential gamification.
     * OpenAI Key is no longer necessary for miners not using an OpenAI LLM, as embedding generation occurs on the validator side now. It is still required to run the testing script, however.
    
    Validators, please update at your earliest convenience to ensure that your scoring is consistent with other Validators. This push is less pressing for miners, but if you are not using OpenAI LLM's, this will help reduce your spend. 
    
    We believe this will have a serious impact on the recent miner UID consolidation that we have observed, and we will continue to monitor the situation and note any changes. As always, please feel free to reach out to me any time with questions or thoughts.

**17:57 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** All,
    
    We have pushed significant updates to address these issues (replied to our latest post on the matter from a few days ago)  With the Bittensor update that was supposed to go live last Monday but is now planned for this week, we should see further improvements. We still have a few validators not up to date and whose scores are artificially high. We have seen top scores coming down to 0.9 range as intended vs. the 0.99 scores that were seen on the high range previously.
    
    We will be pushing out another **two additional changes this week** to address miner concentration. (1) Only registered validators will have access to the API. From the start of the subnet, anyone has had access to the API, but the dataset is infinite as it is pulled from all English language podcasts available through RSS feeds (which is over 2 million different podcasts). (2) We have been rotating a random selection of conversations every interval and we are going to 10x that interval making sharing tags across miner UIDs far less effective.
    
    Over the medium term, we expect more and more queries to come from **organic queries which validators can already do TODAY** and which we are going to enable through our own frontend as well which will make the dataset even more expansive. We have also been developing “dynamic context windows” which we are planning to rollout later this month which, like SN12 and 19, enables miners with more bandwidth to provide that on only 1 UID.
    
    **Our vision is to build a decentralized Scale AI so that anyone via a validator can turn their unstructured data to structured data.** We are still in the first inning of that journey and we have seen incredibly high quality tagging from top miners already. **We are going to be publishing a benchmarking study this week which will show how our top miners are significantly outperforming Mechanic Turk and base GPT models on structured data tasks.**
    
    We have taken all feedback from the community from Day 1 and we will continue to adapt **to make our digital commodity as valuable as possible. That is our long-term focus.**

    <@&1237015679023059017> We just pushed out a new release to the main branch with the following update:
    
    * Changes to update_scores function in base validator class
     * Now applies a non-linear transformation and renormalization to the scores - inspired by Subnet 19's reward mechanism
     * This update will enhance subnet kurtosis and incentivize more miner competition
    * Updates to save_state and load_state
     * enables smooth transition from old validator states to new validator states 
    
    Since our update on 9/9, we have seen a gradual increase in competition between miners that has lead to increased kurtosis in our incentive distribution. Today we build on that momentum by transforming scores and re-normalizing each time the update_scores function is called by validators.

**00:08 jvl:** The purpose of the study was to show our findings that our subnet is outperforming on common benchmarks for annotation both human (MTurk) and LLMs (GPT 4o). We do not know the exact methods used by the miners to achieve top scores, but our template miner has not been able to survive deregistration for many months now. We will adjust the language in the study to reflect this.
    
    To your other points, it is fair play to register multiple UIDs and replicate a method of mining if it is a successful one. Additionally, as you can see in the code, validators write the tags to a database that we administer by default, but are free to write their tags to any DB they choose. We monitor miner tag responses in our Database to check for foul play, and we will push patches when we spot dishonest miner activity, as you can see here: https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1233428828479819876/1276609692965277746 and here: https://discord.com/channels/799672011265015819/1233428828479819876/1268987082920038430. We recently identified other potential gamification vectors and will be pushing out a patch this week to address that as well. Due to bittensor incentive structures, we partake in a constant battle against miner gamification, and are doing the best we can to incentivize honest play. If you have any ideas for how we can better monitor and address these issues, we would love to discuss further and incorporate any solutions that make sense.

### 2024-09-21

**00:40 jvl:** **Subnet Update Announcement**
    
    We have been hard at work this week developing the following updates to the subnet:
    
    * LLM Tag Verification
     * As has been pointed out in the channel, some miners have been able to game the scoring algo through various tag manipulation methods. This is a very difficult problem to solve, and quickly becomes a game of whack-a-mole.
     * We have developed a novel solution using LLMs and prompt-chaining to minimize the effects of this dishonest miner activity. We have seen early successes in our testing that this removes upwards of 90% of dishonest tags.
    * Subnet-wide Default LLM upgrade
     * we have upgraded the default LLM used by both miners and validators to OpenAI GPT-4o
     * this will minimize costs and maximize quality of output. 4o's low cost also enables prompt chaining for LLM verification of miner tags.
     * We will still be enabling miners and validators to choose their own model, should they need to, with a new config variable. Details to come on this shortly
    
    We know that there have been some issues in this subnet with gamification recently, and some members of the community are upset by this. We assure you all that we are taking proactive steps to solve these problems in a permanent way, and as soon as we became aware of the issue, we began developing the fix.
    
    We are hoping to finalize testing over the weekend and deploy this fix on Monday. Thank you all for your patience, and as always please feel free to reach out with questions or concerns.

**20:37 jvl:** Hey, appreciate the note. Many of these tags highlighted are actually not great metadata tags for the purposes of finetuning a model. Regardless, all tags whether filtered by the LLM or not, are written to the Database, so this data is not being thrown out. 
    
    We understand that there are going to be some instances where good tags are going to be thrown out, but in our testing we saw that in 90% of cases, good tags were kept and bad tags were thrown out. The problem that we had to address as a subnet was that a large amount of manipulated and meaningless tags were getting scored, which was both unfair and defeats the purpose of our subnet entirely. This is a very difficult problem to solve, and while it is an imperfect solution, the important thing is that every miner is facing the **same exact filter.** There is no inherent advantage to any individual miner. What this will do over time is incentivize novel ways of finding the **best** tags with the **lowest possible chance** of being filtered by the LLM. Everyone has access to the filter prompt and is free to test their own miner prompts and data tagging techniques against that filter.

**19:46 jvl:** I believe you're missing the concept of "fractal data mining" explained in our readme. The validator's job is to get a ground truth tagging of a full conversation. the miner's job is to receive a window (a small fraction of the full conversation) and perform a more detailed tagging of that window. Window tags are scored by their similarity to the ground truth, but also are incentivized to have completely unique tags through the scoring mechanism. In other words, the miner's job is not to be than the validator, it is to provide a more detailed tagging of the data. Hope this helps

    o Receiving NO requests from ANY validators might not be an issue with the network, or validators: it could be that the miner's ports are not configured correctly.     o Receiving requests from *some* validators, but not all of them, especially not the ones with high stake: this could be an issue on the validator side, which is something the team's been working on for a while, but for now, just knowing that this is the case at least lets us know whether we need to reach out to the validator operators to restart their validators. **19:28 jvl:** **Subnet Update**
    
    <@&1237015679023059017> We are pushing back the closure of the Conversation Server to non-validators to this upcoming Monday, October 14th at 12pm PST. Here are some more details of how this will go down:
    
    **Mainnet:**
     
     * Beginning Monday, we will be enforcing a weights_version hyperparameter. This will require all validators to have a specified version of the repository in order to set weights. 
     * Prior to setting this hyperparameter, we will release an update that prevents validators from setting weights unless they receive a conversation from an API endpoint and query miners - preventing hung validators from setting outdated weights.
     * The weights_version hyperparameter will subsequently be set to the spec version for the release described above.
     * After the updates described above, we will lockdown the API endpoint on our side to only permit validators to access the API
    
    In effect, this will provide 2 major improvements to the subnet: 
     
     * Preventing hung validators from setting outdated weights if they are experiencing problems or errors with their operations, or if they have outdated scoring mechanisms due to future subnet updates
     * Preventing non-validators from accessing the Conversations Server and developing lookup attack methods.
    
    **Testnet:**
    
    As part of our conversations server updates, we will be providing a specific, isolated subset of conversations for testnet operations. Beginning on Monday, Validators with a testnet -compatible API key will be able to query the Conversations Server to receive conversations from this subset. Any Testnet validator with minimum 10tao staked will be able to get a testnet API key. For instructions on how to do this, please see the documentation in docs/generate-validator-api-key.md
    
    As always, please reach out with any questions or thoughts!

    <@&1237015679023059017> Please see information below on 2 major updates occurring next week.
    
    
    **ReadyAI version ~~2.4.23~~ 2.5.25** - Releasing Monday, October 21st at 12pm PST
     * Subnet-wide upgrade to Bittensor version 7.4.0
      * This encompasses updates to the requirements that present package conflicts. As a result, when this update goes live, we strongly recommend you create a fresh venv and reinstall `requirements.txt`
    
    
    **ReadyAI version ~~2.4.24~~ 2.6.26** - Releasing Wednesday, October 23rd at 12pm PST
     * Upgrades to scoring and weight assignment
      * Embeddings Model Upgrade -- we will be upgrading the standard embeddings model from `text-embedding-ada-002` to `text-embedding-3-large`. The upgraded embeddings model presents a significant advancement in semantic meaning capture, allowing us to more accurately score tags submitted by miners. It also provides more variance in tag scores, which bolsters competition in the subnet
      * Rank-based weights -- New rank-based weights will be implemented along with new embeddings to enhance kurtosis
    
    After upgrading to ~~2.4.24~~ 2.6.26, we will be updating the weights_version hyperparameter to match this version as the embeddings model and scoring changes are not backwards-compatible. Validators, please prepare accordingly. The weights_version will be updated at 12pm PST in tandem withe the launch. 
    
    In advance of these updates, we will be updating the activity_cutoff hyperparameter to 720 to prevent outdated weights from impacting miners after the update goes live. 
    
    These updates will provide countless improvements to the competition of the subnet, and allow us to expand the abilities of the subnet to accomodate a wide range of enterprise customers and use-cases.
    
    As always, please reach out with any questions or thoughts!

**18:31 Kat | Fren One:** Closing registration means setting the `registrations_allowed` hyperparameter to `false`.  This prevents anyone from registering. 
    
    Changing the `min_burn` doesn't prevent people from registering, but it makes it expensive to do so.  
    
    Major changes/fixes/updates to the subnet take some time to stabilize.  While that's happening, miners who are on the lower end of the emissions/incentive scale who are out out of their immunity period are vulnerable.  If the issue was due to something that's preventing the validators from properly scoring them, then the devs will increase the `min_burn` to discourage new registrations until the subnet has stabilized, and miners have a chance to be properly scored.

    <@&1237015679023059017> We just pushed out a new release to the main branch with the following updates:
     
     * Upgrades to scoring and weight assignment
      * Embeddings Model Upgrade -- we will be upgrading the standard embeddings model from `text-embedding-ada-002` to `text-embedding-3-large`. The upgraded embeddings model presents a significant advancement in semantic meaning capture, allowing us to more accurately score tags submitted by miners. It also provides more variance in tag scores, which bolsters competition in the subnet
      * Rank-based weights -- New rank-based weights will be implemented along with new embeddings to enhance kurtosis
    
    Validators, we have just updated the weights_version hyperparameter to match the latest version, so please pull the latest branch and restart at your next convenience.
    
    Miners, please note that there are meaningful changes to the scoring system so expect changes to your response scoring and emissions. 
    
    We will be keeping registration costs at 10 tao while we observe the impacts of the upgrade and confirm that it is stable. 
    
    Later today, we will retire all conversations in the database that were present before we closed the API endpoint to validators only.

### 2024-10-31

**15:03 Ivan | Fren One:** Wishing everyone a wonderful Thursday! 😊
**18:43 jvl:** **New Release Live - ReadyAI 2.6.28**
    
    <@&1237015679023059017> We just pushed out a new release to the main branch **for both Validators & Miners** with the following updates:
     * Increase miners per window 
      * Currently, building incentive as a miner takes ~24 hours. By increasing miners per window from 3->6, incentive can be built much quicker, and neurons are much more resilient to outdate/erroneous scores should a validator have an outage or load an outdated state
     * Eliminate Miner Embedding Generation
      * Miners no longer generate embeddings for their tags. Since Version 1.91.14, Validators have been ignoring miner-generated embeddings and generating on their own to prevent dishonest miner activity. Now, miners will no longer generating the embeddings altogether.
      * This should present a meaningful increase to subnet speed and throughput, and decrease miner costs. 
    
    Both of these updates are intended to increase the speed and resiliency of building miner incentive. We have listened to the community and their problems over the last month, and we believe that this is a big step in the right direction. 
    
    To supplement this push, we will be implementing a state check system that will ensure that new or outdated validators do not load a state that is out of consensus. This will curb any impacts that unexpected technical outages or new validator registration has on building miner incentive. Expect this early next week. 
    
    We will be messaging validators to update, however we will not update the weights_version until Monday, November 4th at 12pm PST. Between now and then, updated validators will build scores for new miners at a faster pace than outdated validators, however we do not expect any other impacts from this update, therefore we will not be closing registration.
    
    Thank you all and please feel free to reach out for any questions.

**18:11 rd4Fun:** IMO - miners should monitor the following variables in their registration script:
      `adjustment interval` , `lastAdjustmentBlock`, `RegistrationsThisInterval`,  `burnRegistrationsThisInterval`, `targetregistrationsperinterval`
    
    <https://docs.bittensor.com/subtensor-nodes/subtensor-storage-query-examples#87-targetregistrationsperinterval>
    <https://docs.bittensor.com/subtensor-nodes/subtensor-storage-query-examples#12-burnregistrationsthisinterval>
    <https://docs.bittensor.com/subtensor-nodes/subtensor-storage-query-examples#3-adjustmentinterval>
    <https://docs.bittensor.com/subtensor-nodes/subtensor-storage-query-examples#30-lastadjustmentblock>
    
    Some simple formulas for their script
    Registrations available this interval = targetregistrationsperinterval *3 - burnRegistrationsThisInterval 
    number of blocks until burnRegistrationsThisInterval is reset to 0 =  lastadjustmentblock + adjustmentinterval - current block

**21:30 jvl:** **New Release Live - ReadyAI 2.6.29**
    
    <@&1237015679023059017> We just pushed out a new release to the main branch with an update to the Validator Code.
     
    * Prevent tag-stuffing strategy
      * Randomly select 20 tags from submitted lists greater than 20 prior to tag validation prompt
      * Truncate length of all tags to 50 characters before the tag validation prompt
    
    Earlier today we observed validators submitting thousands of tags per window, which was leading to validators being unable to score any miner windows. As soon as we observed this, we developed a simple solution and tested it on the SN33 Validator. It has been successfully discouraging this strategy and leads to dishonest miners having 0 valid tags in most cases.
    
    Validators, please pull and update at your next convenience. Miners, there is no change to your code but we always advise staying up to date with the latest changes. 
    
    Please reach out if you have any questions about this push.
    
    **Immunity Period Update re: Dec. 11 OpenAI Outage**
    
    We extended our immunity period due to the OpenAI outage and the impact it had on miners yesterday to 9000 blocks. We will be restoring this to 7200 blocks tomorrow at 10AM PST now that the outage is resolved.

    Am I correct in understanding that validators will now reveal weights not once every 360 blocks (72 minutes), but once every 13 hours and 12 minutes?
**14:00 Kat | Fren One:** Yes, that's correct.  A tempo is 360 blocks for all subnets except for subnet 1 (cite: https://docs.bittensor.com/subnets/subnet-hyperparameters#tempo ).  Therefore, the commit reveal interval being set to 11 means that the reveal will happen after 3960 blocks.  Assuming a block time of 12 s, that means that it will happen after 47,520 seconds (i.e., 792 minutes or 13.2 hours).  Ish, though, because not all blocks are finalized in 12 seconds.
**19:49 jvl:** Actually, this is not quite right. The pace at which validators set weights will not be changed. What will change is when those weights become visible on chain: this will happen 11 intervals later. For example, if a vali sets weights in interval 1, those weights will become visible in interval 12. The weights they set in interval 2 will become visible in interval 13, weights in interval 3 become visible in interval 14, so on and so forth.
**19:50 jvl:** The point of commit reveal is to put weight copying validators out of sync with the rest of the honest validators, which would impact their earnings, removing the economic incentive to copy weights.

    SN33 Community,
    
    A misleading report on SN33 has been published and we would like to clear the air regarding some of the accusations made in his article. The author alleges that SN33 is being exploited by a single miner through a theoretical attack vector, that we have not made meaningful developments to the subnet in 6 months, and that we have made empty promises regarding developments to the subnet.
    
    The author of this post deduces that SN33 is monopolized by a single miner with access to a pre-processed database of tagged conversations from a single proof point: Identical results across some conversation windows from multiple miner hotkeys.
    
    We have taken all claims of potential exploits very seriously as a subnet team. It is irresponsible to assume that what the author alleges based on a single observation is true, however, Bittensor is a constantly adversarial environment, and we have dealt with gamification of the subnet (as has nearly every other subnet in the ecosystem) since we first launched the subnet in May. As you can see by the following Merged PRs: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged+ we have taken an active stance in addressing these exploits as they come up. 
    
    While we continue to not have any clear evidence outside of this being a theoretical attack vector and not one actively being exploited, **we will be pushing a fix in the next 24 hours that directly addresses the miners concern implementing their suggested solution: Retrieve many conversations at once and send random windows from random conversations.**
    
    From a development perspective, in Q4 2024, we have been prioritizing building an open-source Data Structuring Jobs interface and a Web application leveraging the subnet. This gives end users access to a decentralized Scale AI to generate structured data for their AI models and RAG systems. We have already demoed this for a number of validators and at the DCG Bittensor Summit and have received great feedback and plan to release the v1 this month. In combination with the engineering efforts to ship this complex system, we have dedicated time and resources to business development and building out demos for generating sales leads. Our mission is to make ReadyAI a core part of the decentralized AI stack, and lead the way in monetization of the digital commodities on BIttensor.
    
    The author of this post, who admitted to controlling the majority of keys in the subnet at one point (and raised no issue with our subnet then), brought this theoretical exploit to us on December 19th, at which point we made no guarantees to deliver what they were requesting. Candidly, we feel that while there is room for improvement in the subnet, it is much more likely that these complaints come from a disgruntled miner with a vested interest in the subnet operating in line with their own financial benefit. The miner made various threats to share information about the potential exploit, which we felt was in extremely bad faith and further aligned with our thinking that this was a disgruntled lone wolf.

**01:14 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** There were a number of other misleading and inaccurate claims made in the piece. Below we will address them individually:
    
    Claim: “I was told that the creators personally know all the validators and that if a miner (specifically me) made such an attempt, it would end poorly only for me”
    
    **Response**: We never said this. The miner made a threat to share inaccurate information with validators in an attempt to hold our subnet hostage for the developments that fit his personal agenda, and we responded that this was not an effective way of proposing changes to the subnet.
    
    Claim: “an update was released that resulted in validators no longer displaying their logs on WandB.”
    
    **Response**: This is not true, the logs of validators who enable logging on wandb are available here: https://wandb.ai/afterparty/conversationgenome. In line with many other subnets, validators are free to log or not log to wandb. 
    
    Claim: “The subnet creators failed to meet their promises to fix the exploit within their self-imposed deadline.”
    
    **Response**: We did not offer any concrete timeline on the suggestions provided by the author of this post. We agreed to review their suggestions.
    
    Claim: At present, Subnet 33 serves no meaningful purpose. A single monopolizing miner dominates the network, generates low-quality tags, and profits without driving any innovation.
    
    **Response**: This is a wildly unsubstantiated and subjective claim. We provide high-quality tags, monitoring the quality of these tags consistently and are currently developing a wide expansion of the system to include other job types besides tagging. There is no convincing evidence of a single party dominating the subnet. 
    
    Claim: The validator code already supports multiple LLMs, but the implementation is broken due to incompatible tag formats. 
    
    **Response**: This is false, validators can run on any of the LLMs that we support on the subnet. Currently Testnet Validator UID 58 is running on Groq Llama3 8B. There are not “incompatible tag formats” - tags are generated, stored in text in a CSV, and then passed to the validator regardless of source LLM. 
    
    Please continue to provide your feedback to us.

**05:12 mark86118:** <@750809532334080060> <@538101635478454272> First thanks for the fix - I want to point out though that **the main "exploit" is still available**.
    
    The conversation_guid and the window_idx are still present in the synapse sent to miners, so all miners still have access to them (just removing the logs doesn't change anything, you can still access and store the information easily).
    In case you didn't fully grasp the issue let me explain again. People with a large number of miners have an advantage over new comers. This is because when you have a lot of miners, you can expect that each request will reach at least one of your miners. You can then keep the conversation window using the conversation guid, sort it using the window index, and use all that information from another miner when they receive another window for the same conversation, hence giving you an advantage by having more context. 
    How to fix it? Remove the conversation_guid and window_idx from the following line 
    `window_packet = {"guid":conversation_guid, "window_idx":window_idx, "lines":conversation_window}`
    
    Until then, your fix doesn't mitigate the exploit, and you're still in the same state as the report that has been shared above, which is one or two miners only exploiting the subnet.
**06:08 jvl:** Thank you for your message. We have yet to see any real evidence that this exploit is being conducted by any mining parties, but we can offer some clarity regarding the conversation GUID. These are temporary, generated once every time the conversation is retrieved from the API. When the conversation is retrieved and given a temporary guid, 5 conversation windows are then selected shuffled between 10 different conversations. This means that while a validator is working through 50 windows, only 5 of them are coming from a single GUID. The method you just described wouldn't give much advantage at all - you would be working with 5 randomly assorted, disconjoined slivers of conversations. The next time the conversation is retrieved, there would be a different GUID.
    
    That being said, we will be pushing another update next week with further updates for security to the subnet, and we will take the suggestion of eliminating the GUID altogether into consideration.

### 2025-01-31

**01:01 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** SUBNET ANNOUNCEMENT
    
    <@&1237015679023059017> We have recently observed some strange weight-setting patterns among both honest and weight-copying validators. It appears that new miners are facing a sharp decrease in their weights roughly 13.5 hours into their registration. This coincides with the end of the CR Interval of 11 tempos. 
    
    To summarize what we're seeing: in honest validators, we see the weights slowly build after registration as expected, and take a steep dive at the next weight-set after the CR Interval has elapsed. In weight-copying validators, we see the weights from the previous UID holder being copied (most likely due to CR interval delay), and then the weights decreasing sharply once the initial weights from honest validators are revealed (they are now copying scores from early in the miner's registration). 
    
    The weight copying is problematic, however we understand the root cause of it. We are working now to understand how CR might be impacting the honest validator's scoring, and why there is a dip around the end of the CR interval. 
    
    We had hoped that Commit Reveal would curtail weight copying in our subnet, however it is clear that the efforts have come short, given that weight copying is still causing problems in the subnet. While we investigate, we will be temporarily disabling Commit Reveal to observe if the score fluctuations in honest validators are correlated with CR being enabled. In the coming days we may also temporarily re-enable it with varying intervals to observe the effects on the subnet. 
    
    Thanks for you understanding, and thank you to our miner community for flagging this strange behavior. Please reach out it you have any questions!

    ## **ReadyAI 2.0 is here\! AI-Ready Data with the Jobs Interface**
    
    ReadyAI just launched our **Jobs Interface Beta**, a powerful frontend that enables organic queries on Subnet 33\. This new interface allows end users to process raw data from any Huggingface dataset into structured outputs tailored to their needs. Try it now: www.readyai.ai
    
    This milestone is a significant step toward our vision of becoming a **decentralized Scale AI**. ReadyAI empowers individual developers and enterprises of all sizes to make their data AI-ready, seamlessly integrating it into AI models and applications.
    
    ### **Organic Queries: The Next Era for the ReadyAI Ecosystem**
    
    We have initiated the next phase of our journey with the introduction of **organic queries** into the miner incentive system. This phased rollout ensures:
    
    * **Fair Miner Scoring**: Maintaining fairness and high-quality outputs for all contributors.  
    * **Structured Data Integration**: All Tagging queries processed through the Jobs Interface will now be scored alongside conversation data.  
    * **New Data Sources**: Social media data, starting with SN13 Dataverse Reddit data, will be incorporated as an organic query source.
    
    Data tagging and structuring are pivotal steps in the AI Agent pipeline. With the increasing demand for real-time, high-quality data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems and fine-tuned models, ReadyAI is uniquely positioned to lead this transformation. Over the next couple of months, we will showcase AI Agents powered by our structured data pipeline.
**18:19 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** ## **3–6 Month Roadmap**
    
    ### **1\. Organic Queries / Jobs Interface**
    
    * **Initial Rollout**: Organic Tagging queries are live via the Jobs Interface on www.readyai.ai right now and are being processed by the ReadyAI validator.  
      * These queries currently account for 1–5% of total validator windows.  
      * Other validators may adopt this new branch, but we will be testing with ours to ensure vTrust and tag quality remains high before rolling this out more broadly.  
      * These tagging jobs are being processed in parallel by the mainnet validator and private worker nodes operated by the ReadyAI team in order to evaluate subnet tagging results.   
    * **Social Media Data Expansion**: After validating the initial rollout, we plan to increase the proportion of validator windows processed from social media datasets from Macrocosmos Dataverse (SN13).
    
    ### **2\. Incentive Design 2.0**
    
    * **Enhanced Capabilities**: We are upgrading our incentive system to support metadata tagging for arbitrary text data. This includes:  
      * Single-label and multi-label categorization.  
      * Expanding beyond the current category tagging capabilities including image.  
    * **Competitive Positioning**: These improvements will achieve product parity with Scale AI's structured data offerings, reinforcing ReadyAI's position as a high-quality, cost-effective alternative.

**18:53 Kat | Fren One:** Yes.  When you set up a miner, you need to choose an LLM service. **02:09 papercirer:** Thanks for bringing this up. It’s a valid concern and one we addressed from miner feedback in early January (check the pinned posts) as part of the ongoing design of the subnet.
    
    **Here’s how it works right now:**
    - The validator receives 10 random conversations from the Ready AI API.
    - It selects 5 random windows from each conversation.
    - The 50 windows are shuffled and 6 random windows are sent to 6 random miners (1 per miner).
    - So while it’s technically possible for a miner with many identities to receive multiple windows from the same conversation in a single round, they don’t have a clear way to identify it is part of the same conversation and the odds are relatively low due to the double randomness (both in conversation and window selection), and even lower over the long term.
    
    **We believe the current setting of `num_windows_per_convo = 5` strikes a good balance:**
    - It helps increase the chances that different parts of a convo get tagged.
    - improves coverage and model understanding of full conversations.
    
    **Looking ahead, our roadmap includes a refinement of this selection logic. We plan to move toward a more controlled sampling strategy that:**
    1. Ensures comprehensive tagging coverage across entire conversations over time.
    2. Prevents multiple windows from the same conversation from being sent in the same challenge loop.
    
    
    Questions like this are very helpful for everyone here 🙂 Hope it answers your question!
**02:19 CryptoMonkey:** Thanks for the clarification. Alright, I see that the windows are shuffled — however, it's still relatively easy to cluster windows that originate from the same conversation. Since they tend to share many overlapping tags, one could apply something like k-NN on the tag embeddings to group them. While this approach may not yield perfect accuracy, it can still be highly effective and consistently identify windows from the same convo with strong confidence.
**02:24 CryptoMonkey:** Also, it appears that the top miner already operates with 200+ hotkeys. At that scale, they can easily capture all 50 windows in a single validation round. This creates a significant structural advantage that's difficult to overcome through model quality alone.
**02:27 CryptoMonkey:** If you really want to keep num_windows_per_convo = 5, could you please consider increasing the number of miners selected per window? For example, instead of sending each request to just 6 miners, expanding it to 30 could help reduce the advantage held by miners with massive scale, and give newer or smaller participants a more fair chance to compete based on model quality.
**02:28 CryptoMonkey:** in that sense, people with 20 hotkeys can compete with people with 200 hotkeys

    Each validation loop sends out 50 windows in total — that's 5 random windows from each of 10 conversations. Each of those windows is sent to 6 randomly selected miners.
    
    So technically, a miner with a large number of hotkeys could receive multiple windows in a single round.
    
    We'll take some time to look into the suggestion and see how we can improve going forward.

**00:20 Nadezhda:** Hello. Can I work as a human in manual labor in this subnet, for example checking annotated data, and get paid for this work? It was written somewhere that ReadyAI uses a symbiosis of human intuition and automation to create high-quality structured data for AI.
**11:11 Nadezhda:** <@188485281148698624>  Can you help me with this question? 👆
**13:35 papercirer:** Yes for sure! 
    
    Well first of all, I think it's important to clarify how subnet 33 and Bittensor actually work
    
    Bittensor is a decentralized system where miners compete by providing high-quality outputs. Here in subnet 33, the output is tags for specific parts of conversations. They sre then scored by validators based on uniqueness and relevance.
    
    The key point is **competition**: miners are constantly racing to produce the best results faster and more effectively than others, many of whom are running highly optimized machine learning models or algorithms.
    
    So, while it could be possible to contribute manually (like checking or annotating data by hand), in practice, **you would not be able to compete as a human doing manual labor**. 
    
    The speed, consistency, and scale of automated systems surpass what a person could do manually.
    
    If you're interested in mining, you'd likely need to build or run a system that can do this work autonomously or semi-autonomously. Manual human effort might still play a role in *training* or *improving* such systems, but not directly as a miner or validator on subnet 33.
    
    Hope this answers your question 🙂
**18:09 Nadezhda:** Yes, thank you very much, I got an answer to some aspects of my question. 
    
    But I would like to clarify one more thing, if you allow me, you wrote: "Manual human effort might still play a role in training or improving such systems, but not directly as a miner or validator on subnet 33".
    
    How can I participate in this project with manual labor not as a miner and validator?
**18:18 papercirer:** Glad it answered some parts of it 😛
    
    You can totally be a part of the project by being a miner and a validator!
    
    What I meant is that, you need to channel your manual labor to craft highly optimized machine learning models or algorithms.
    
    Then you can compete with the current miners in the ecosystem.
    
    If you try to compete with the miner only by the sheer power of your manual labor, like by tagging the conversations manually yourself, it won't do!
    You need to leverage automation, AI and computers to be able to compete!

**17:17 papercirer:** # 🚀 **Improved Local Testing Is Here — Powered by MOT33** 🧠
    
    We’ve upgraded Subnet 33’s **Miner Optimization Toolkit (MOT33)** to give miners **more control** — and to ensure that the local testing API now uses **conversations generated the same way as in production**, just like the ones **validators receive** and **send to miners** during actual runs.
    
    ## 🛠️ **What’s New**
    
    - ✅ **Local API now uses our real, spoken podcast dataset** — pulled directly from our Hugging Face dataset, which contains conversations generated **with the exact same pipeline** used in the validator flow:  [`ReadyAi/5000-podcast-conversations-with-metadata-and-embedding-dataset`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ReadyAi/5000-podcast-conversations-with-metadata-and-embedding-dataset)
    - 🎯 **You can now test on specific conversations** to track improvements more precisely.
    
    ## 📰 **Hosted API vs Local API**
    
    - **Hosted Test API** (default):  
      - Returns realistic podcast-style conversations.  
      - Limited to a fixed pool of ~300.  
      - No control over which one you receive.  
    
    - **Local API**:  
      - Pulls the full dataset from Hugging Face automatically.  
      - Lets you lock to a specific conversation.  
      - Ideal for iteration, benchmarking, and debugging.
    
    ## 🧪 **How to Use It**
    
    - 🔧 [Run quick local tests using the hosted API](https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project?tab=readme-ov-file#quickstart-mock-tests)  
    - 🌐 [Run the full local API with Hugging Face dataset](https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project?tab=readme-ov-file#validating-with-a-custom-conversation-server)
    
    Give it a try — and let us know how it helps you build better miners!
    If you want to see specific improvements, let us know 🙂

**00:05 papercirer:** # 🚀 Local Testing Upgrade – Powered by MOT33 – Release 1.4
    
    v1.4 of the **Miner Optimization Toolkit (MOT33)** is now live on Docker Hub!  
    This release adds **support for connecting to a local subtensor chain**, giving you more **flexibility and control** in your local development loop.
    
    ## Why It Matters  
    You can now test your **miner**, **validator**, and **API** in a **fully local stack** by pointing them to a subtensor chain running on your machine.
    
    Just adjust the environment variables to target your local chain, and you're ready to test.  
    More details on how to deploy a local chain:  https://docs.bittensor.com/local-build/deploy
    
    This unlocks:
    - Full end-to-end testing loops  
    - Faster iteration and deeper debugging  
    - Offline or isolated development without relying on public infrastructure
    
    Perfect for those who want to test and fine-tune every component in a custom environment.
    
    ## Also in v1.4
    
    - Improved DockerHub documentation with clear steps for launching miners, validators and APIs from the image!
    - Simplified `.env` configuration with easy overrides for fast experimentation
    
    ## What You Can Do With the Image
    
    - Run a **CGP API** preloaded with real conversations  
    - Run a **validator** using a local or self-hosted API  
    - Run a **miner**  
    - Connect all components to a **local subtensor chain** (you run the chain, the image connects)
    
    ## Docs & Setup Guide  
    The image is available here: https://hub.docker.com/r/readyai/bittensor-readyai-sn33
    
    Give it a shot and let us know what you'd like to see next! 🙂

**01:30 papercirer:** ## 🔁 **Auto-Rotating W&B Logs - Update for Validators - v2.10.45**
    
    We've just released an important update to improve validator logging stability:  
    **Automatic WandB run rotation** is now supported to ensure validators never hit the **100,000-line log limit** in WandB runs.
    
    ### Why It Matters
    Validators with long-running sessions were previously losing logs when reaching 100k lines.
    With this update, validators will **automatically start a new run** before hitting the limit — ensuring miners can always view your logs for visibility, trust, and debugging.p
    
    This change:
    - Prevents log loss
    - Keeps logs flowing for miners to inspect validator behavior  
    - Enhances overall transparency across the subnet  
    
    ### Strongly Recommended
    This update is **not mandatory**, but we **strongly encourage all validators to upgrade** to support the best possible ecosystem experience for miners.
    
    ReadyAI's Validator has been updated to this new version!
    
    ### How It Works
    The rotation triggers after 90,000 lines and seamlessly starts a new run while preserving continuous logging behavior.  
    No config changes required. Just pull the latest code and restart your process!
    
    Let's log 🪵

**22:44 papercirer:** Hey Purge, first of all thanks for voicing your observations!
    
    Before we talk specifics, we have to keep in mind the subnet's goals which are to create an environment where miners can compete to optimize and innovate. 
    We want them to create the best tags for conversations. All our decisions are made with that in mind.
    
    That being said, here is what I have to say:
    
    - Releasing validators' tags would incentivize overfitting
        - Instead of really competing for the best tags, miners would start optimizing for tags that match the validators' tags.
        - It will be a matter of time before we see convergence toward the validators' output instead of diverse, high-quality tagging strategies.
    - Releasing miners' tags would not level the playing field
        - Transparency here would undermine fair competition
        - It would allow miners to copy what top miners do and defeat the purpose of the subnet.
    - On the quality of tags:
        - I am not sure I understand your concern here. GPT-4 level of quality seems pretty good to me
        - I would be happy to clarify if you can elaborate
    - On sending the windows to more miners:
        - I am curious about the reasoning here. Increasing the number of miners would only increase overall load across the subnet without a clear benefit to scoring.
        - How would that improve competitiveness?
            - If a miner is unable to compete now, why would that change with that increase?
    
    Hope it answers some of your questions and creates new ones 🙂

**15:53 Dreander:** Hey! Thanks so much for the feedback — that’s a really good point! Let me try to explain why this is done during annotation:
    
    Splitting text into overlapping chunks is actually a standard practice in annotation. Without overlap, you might get a question in one chunk and the answer in the next — and the model has no chance to see them together. By adding overlap, we’re essentially annotating with some buffer, including context from both the left and right. So removing the overlap would actually lower the quality of the annotations.
    
    As for the window collection — it’s a bit tricky. The windows are selected randomly, so they rarely end up next to each other or overlapping. Plus, only 10 conversations are sampled at a time. We could ask the devs to bump that number up by 10x to make the process more robust. If it’s feasible
**17:16 papercirer:** As the miners don't need the overlapping context and the validators have the whole conversation to generate the ground truth tags. 
    
    Do you think the impact of removing the overlap would actually be that big?
**18:58 Dreander:** I don’t quite understand how this would impact the miners, but it would definitely negatively affect the original idea behind subnet 33.
    
    The initial concept was detailed, window-level annotation. Ideally, each window should include a bit of context on both sides to be labeled properly.
    The overlaps are there to prevent abrupt cuts in conversation. Even if only one miner (either to the left or right) gets that extra context, it significantly improves the annotation quality.
    
    Right now, I don’t see a way to collect windows reliably at the moment, but if there are concerns about this, I’d suggest increasing the number of conversations per pass from 10 to 20 or even 50.

**09:12 Dreander:** Unfortunately, from a practical standpoint, what you’re proposing would actually harm ReadyAI, because the lines are being cut randomly, and you may lose important tags as a result.
    
    Let me give you an example:
    In the first part, a person might talk about a certain topic, and in the second part, they refer to it using just “it.” If you’re unlucky with where the cut happens and there’s no overlap, neither window will have enough context.
    For instance, they might mention weight loss and then talk about accepting it or going through various emotional stages related to it. The isolated windows might end up with generic tags like “fasting,” “weight loss,” “acceptance,” or “psychology.”
    But if there’s even a small overlap, at least one window could be tagged with more meaningful and precise concepts like “body acceptance” or “body positivity.”
    
    So overlaps weren’t added just for fun — they’re a core requirement by design.
**09:16 Dreander:** And simply increasing the window size doesn’t really solve this issue — unless you send the entire conversation, which would defeat the purpose of subnet33 altogether.

    Here's my thinking:
    when a miner has processed lots of conversations during his minig, they develop a strong "predictive advantage" for those 2-line overlaps.

**22:34 papercirer:** # 🚀 Dampening the Impact of Zero Scores - Validator Update - v2.11.46
    We've just released an important update to improve validator and miner experience!
    
    ## ⚠️ Mandatory Update ⚠️
    This update is mandatory for all validators.
    Please upgrade as soon as possible to ensure consistent behavior across the network and to maintain the best possible experience for miners.
    **ReadyAI's validator has already been updated to this new version!**
    
    ## What's new?
    - When a miner's score for a window is exactly zero, we now reduce the alpha (update rate) in the EMA (Exponential Moving Average) calculation.
    - This means zero scores on windows will have less immediate impact, but your overall score will still decay gradually if issues persist.
    
    ## Why this change?
    - Sometimes, zero scores can happen due to temporary network issues, overloads, or other random problems that aren't directly the miner's fault.
    - By dampening the effect of zero rewards, we make the score updates more stable and avoid harsh penalties from short-term glitches.
    - Miners facing temporary problems will now get deregistered more slowly, giving them more time to recover before losing their spot.
    - Reducing the impact of zero scores also helps decrease the variance of miner scores accross different validators, leading to a more consistent vtrust level on the network.
    
    As always, keep an eye on your miner's performance. 
    
    Feel free to reach out if you have any questions! 🫡
    
    Happy mining  ⛏️

**20:33 papercirer:** To circle back on the concerns regarding validator API keys. This is something we take very seriously and have taken a number of measures to date to mitigate this concern (validator verification for API keys, periodic monitoring of API for unusual behavior and regular retiring of conversations from the API). While the Bittensor ecosystem as a whole relies on trust in validators, it’s equally important to have safeguards in place to maintain a fair and transparent environment.
    
    After internal discussions with the team, we will:
    - Add continuous monitoring to detect unusual or suspicious behavior on the API, and
    - Make API usage data publicly visible to ensure transparency for the community.
    
    To further reduce the potential advantage of caching or hoarding full conversations, we’re also planning to dramatically increase the number of daily transcriptions and daily conversation retirements. This will further limit the window of opportunity for any validator-miner pair attempting to reverse-engineer or pre-tag content.
    
    Our goal is to ensure a fair and competitive environment for all miners. We appreciate you bringing this up. If you have other ideas or notice anything suspicious, please don’t hesitate to share.

**19:38 Kat | Fren One:** Also, another thing to monitor is the wandb table (here: https://wandb.ai/afterparty/conversationgenome/table ) -- you can use this to monitor your UID's actual scores from the validators.  This factors into your emissions; nodes with lower emissions are going to be deregistered first (once out of immunity).
    (embed) afterparty
    Weights & Biases, developer tools for machine learning
**19:41 Kat | Fren One:** Yes, that is correct; if you've been deregistered, you will have to register again, and registration costs are burned (they are not refunded).
    
    As to *why*, there is no single reason other than "your node was at the bottom of the emissions list"; the nodes at the bottom of the emissions ranking are going to be the first ones deregistered.
    
    It's a competitive subnet; if you do not fine-tune your miner (if you're using the base model), that's a likely reason to be deregistered, especially if you are looking at your miner logs and you're seeing good communication between your miner and the validators.
**19:42 Kat | Fren One:** So, basically, if you do `btcli s show` and your UID is consistently at the bottom in the "Emissions" column, you'd be vulnerable.  I *think* that Taostats will also mark UIDs that are likely to be deregistered.
**19:45 Kat | Fren One:** No, the "immunity" extrinsic can be set by the subnet owner.  `btcli s hyperparameters --netuid 33` will get you the current hyperparameters for subnet 33; for this subnet, the `immunity_period` is 7200 blocks, which is approximately one day (24 hours) at a ~12-sec block time.
**19:46 Kat | Fren One:** As for the "Danger" marking -- I'm not sure, as Taostats is a third-party service, but that sounds about right to me.
**19:46 Kat | Fren One:** If you are on Taostats and sort the subnet's participants by the "emissions" column, the UIDs at the bottom of the list that are out of immunity are the ones in danger.
**19:50 Kat | Fren One:** As for a set time window, I'm not sure about that.  You could ask Taostats directly in their Discord server: https://discord.gg/9M6NRgNufY (it might already be posted there in some kind of faq channel).  You can verify this link in the <#1215386737661055056> channel (in the "Useful Links" article) before clicking -- I would encourage that, always. : )
**19:55 Kat | Fren One:** Here's something else I'd recommend: search this channel by the phrase "fine-tune", but then type "in:33" and select this subnet channel from the list of channels that come up.  That will find you everything that's been posted with "fine-tune" in it, which might get you started on working on fine-tuning.
    
    Also, a pro tip: if you register both a validator and a miner on **testnet** (netuid 138), you'll have access to the logs of each.  So you'll be able to monitor how your fine-tuning changes the validator's ranking of your miner (and when wandb picks up your miner on testnet, you'll be able to use that to monitor your scores too).
**19:56 Kat | Fren One:** Now: the scoring on testnet will not be realistic (if you run a validator, that means there will probably be a grand total of two validators on testnet), but at least you'll be able to understand more of the process of validator comms and scoring, and see what kinds of impact your fine-tuning might have.

**17:19 papercirer:** # 🚀  Automatic Request Retries – Validator Update – `v2.12.47`
    
    We've just shipped a reliability-focused update to the validator that improves how handle transient miner errors are handled during validation!
    
    Validators now automatically retry failed synapses exactly once for miner axons that return specific transient errors like 408 (timeout) or 422.
    This makes the network more robust in the face of momentary miner hiccups.
    
    ## ⚠️ Mandatory Update
    
    **This update is mandatory for all validators.**
    Please upgrade as soon as possible to ensure consistency across the network and prevent score discrepancies.
    ReadyAI's validator has already been upgraded to this version.
    
    ### Key improvements:
    
    - Detects failed axon responses with `status_code == 408` or `422`.
    - Retries once for affected miners within the same validation pass.
    - Includes logs to track retries and responses status codes.
    
    ### Why this change?
    
    This update helps ensure:
    - Fairer validation outcomes for all miners
    - Less score variance overall
    - An overall smoother experience for miners
    
    As always, keep an eye on your logs and your miner performance!
    Questions? Drop them in the chat, we're here to help.
    
    Thank you and happy mining  ⛏️

**19:05 papercirer:** # 🚀  Validator Update: Handling Empty Tag Responses - `v2.13.48` <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    Hey! We've just pushed a small but important update to the validator code.
    
    Some miners were returning successful (200) responses without any tags, which previously caused unexpected behavior on the validator side
    
    ## ⚠️ Mandatory Update,
    **This update is mandatory for all validators.**
    Please upgrade as soon as possible to ensure consistency across the network and prevent score discrepancies.
    -> ReadyAI's validator has already been upgraded to this version.
    
    ## What changed:
    A safeguard has been added to gracefully handle an empty tags response from a miner.
    -> Keep in mind, your miner will receive a score of 0 for the current window if no tags are returned to the validator.
    
    ## Why this change:
    - Prevents errors due to empty tag responses
    - Ensures more stable validation cycles
    - Improves robustness
    
    Keep an eye on your miners, thank you and happy mining ⛏️

**21:32 Kat | Fren One:** One of the things you might consider doing -- if you have the resources to support it -- is run your own validator on testnet also.  Not only will your miner get queried more quickly, but you'll have access to its logs.  And you should be able to modify the code so it only queries your miner, so you'll see the conversation build up more quickly.
    
    The scores all factor into your ranking in the subnet.  If you compare the individual validator scores against the info you get from the metagraph (`btcli s metagraph --network test --netuid 138`), you should be able to see some trends there with respect to what weights your miner is getting.  
    
    However, understand that testnet is really just there for you to verify that your miner is up and running, receiving requests and submitting tags, and also to give you a rough sense of scoring.  It's not really going to give you any information to let you know whether or not your miner would be competitive on mainnet (which is very competitive).
