**21:04 papercirer:** ## Dynamic Prompt Support – Update for Miners & Validators – v2.14.49
    
    We've released an update that takes the first steps toward sending many different task types to miners.
    
    **Why It Matters**
    Currently, miners all receive the same type of tasks. In the future, validators will also send different tasks such as:
    - Metadata generation for Common Crawl webpages
    - Sentiment analysis
    - Content safety classification
    
    This will allow the subnet to process a much wider variety of data and expand miner capabilities.
    
    **This release:**
    - **Adds dynamic prompt support**: Validators now send the prompt to miners instead of it being hardcoded.
        - **Right now**: The prompt is the same as before, so behavior doesn't change yet.
    
    ReadyAI's validator has been running Common Crawl webpage tagging tasks for some time. Instead of conversation windows, these tasks use markdown slices of real webpages, which miners tag in the same way as conversation text.
    ➡️ As of today's release, all validators on Subnet 33 can now issue these tasks network-wide.
    
    **Looking Ahead**
    The goal is to send the entire task definition dynamically so miners can handle any type of work we send.
    
    For each task, validators will send a `prompt_chain`. It is a suggested baseline approach miners can follow. You're still free to implement your own method, and in fact, creative approaches are highly encouraged and may or may not perform better in the subnet competition for incentives.
    
    *When we move to full dynamic tasks, there will be a breaking change. We'll give notice in advance before that happens.*
    
    **Recommended Action**
    This update is not mandatory, but we strongly encourage miners and validators to upgrade now.
    > ReadyAI's validator is already running this version.
    
    **How to Upgrade**
    Pull the latest code and restart. No config changes required.
    
    This is a first big step toward a more flexible, multi-task subnet.
    
    ⛏️ Happy mining!

### 2025-09-03

**21:39 papercirer:** ## Upcoming Release – Initial Task Types & Default Prompts – v2.17.52  <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    We're preparing to roll out an update **early next week** that lays the groundwork for full **task-based execution** in Subnet 33.  
    
    ## Why It Matters  
    This release takes the next step toward validators being able to send a wide variety of task types to miners.  
    
    It introduces:  
    - **Initial task types**:  
      - `conversation_tagging` → same as current behavior (miners tag conversation windows).  
      - `webpage_metadata_generation` → miners receive a webpage in Markdown form and must generate metadata tags that represent the content of that page.
            - You can see the intial default prompt for the task here: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/90/files#diff-d1a588da417c6887674ca593326b3fbad99bf0b61826f8160420044e29110f52R5-R7
    - **Task-specific default prompts** so miners always have a safe fallback if no prompt is provided.  
    - **Validator propagation of task type** alongside conversation windows.  
    
    These changes are **non-breaking**. Miners without task-specific logic will continue working as before.  
    
    ## Why This Empowers Miners  
    From this release onward, the **power is in your hands**:  
    - Validators will pass a `task_type` with each request.  
    - Miners can choose to **adjust their behavior** depending on the type of task.  
    - You're free to innovate!
    
    ## Looking Ahead  
    Future releases will expand supported task types and introduce full `prompt_chain` definitions.  
    > ⚠️ The release AFTER this one will be a breaking change, but we'll provide clear notice before it happens.  
    
    ## Recommended Action  
    Once v2.17.52 is out, we strongly encourage all miners and validators to upgrade promptly to stay aligned. 
    
    PR is available here: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/90
    
    ⛏️ The rollout will be early next week. This is the bridge to truly **multi-task mining**. Stay tuned!

**14:58 Cookie Monster:** On the contrary - the current system already creates a natural incentive structure. The majority of rewards go to the top miners, while lower-scoring miners still earn something, albeit a small share compared to the high registration cost. This balance is what makes it a true competition. Completely removing rewards for non-top miners would destroy motivation altogether.
    
    Right now, motivation remains extremely high: during the immunity period, low miners can only recover a small fraction of their registration fee. This creates pressure to improve performance, while still giving them a chance to participate and learn. It’s a delicate mechanism that aligns incentives.
    
    If the registration cost were artificially lowered and rewards limited only to the very top miners, the competition would collapse - as has been observed repeatedly in neighboring subnets. When weaker miners are driven out entirely, participation shrinks, quality plummets, and organizers end up with low-value tags.
    
    The economics are clear: healthy competition requires both a strong top tier and a motivated lower tier striving to improve. Undermining that balance by cutting rewards and slashing entry costs would devalue the entire process and weaken the subnet in the long run

**17:59 papercirer:** Hey, I got news from the team, here it is:
    
    The reason you're seeing `Invalid signature: Signature bytes not marked as a schnorrkel signature` is that our verifier only accepts sr25519 Substrate accounts right now.
    
    Ledger accounts exposed through Talisman are usually ed25519-ledger, so schnorrkel rejects them. That's why the sig won't verify even though you're holding TAO just fine.
    
    **Workaround today**: Move some TAO from your Ledger account into an sr25519 Substrate account in Talisman/Polkadot.js. That sr25519 account will pass verification.
    
    **Coming update**: We're adding support for ed25519-ledger accounts in the verifier. Once that's live, you'll be able to sign directly with your Ledger TAO account without moving funds. Until then, sr25519 is the only supported key type for login/verification.
    
    The update should be released next week.

    I'd recommend reading the error messages.  For most package dependencies, the error will actually tell you what you need to do, or at least get you in the ballpark.  Then, use a search engine to search on the key terms from the error plus whatever you're using (e.g., `soemthing or other error ubuntu 22.04`).  You'll most likely find a thread on Stack Overflow or Reddit that will give you the solution. : )

**20:13 papercirer:** ### 🚀 ⚠️  Upcoming Mandatory Release - Task/Bundle Refactor - v2.18.53 <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    We will be rolling out a **breaking release** that restructures the validator/miner code so that logic now lives in the domain classes (Tasks, TaskBundles, and ScoringMechanisms).  
    This is another step towards running many more task types in Subnet 33.  
    
    This upgrade is **mandatory**. __Older versions will stop working once this goes live.__  
    
    When? `September 30th 2025`
    
    The PR is here: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/92
    
    ### What's New
    - **Task / TaskBundle architecture**  
      - All domain logic (conversation slicing, metadata, scoring context) is now delegated to Task and Task Bundle classes.
      - Validators just orchestrate.
    
    - **Pluggable scoring mechanisms**  
      - New `ScoringMechanism` interface.  
      - First implementation: `GroundTruthTagSimilarityScoringMechanism`, which is the current way of scoring.
    
    - **Initial task types**  
      - `conversation_tagging` → miners tag conversation windows (same as before).  
      - `webpage_metadata_generation` → miners receive a webpage in Markdown and generate metadata tags describing its content.  
    
    ### Why It Matters
    - New tasks can be added without disruptive rewrites.  
    - All mining logic now lives inside the Tasks and miners can easily adjust behavior.
    - The system becomes cleaner and more maintainable.
    
    ### Looking Ahead
    - **Prompt Chains are next.**  
      The next release will introduce full prompt-chain definitions, letting validators send *task-specific, multi-step instructions* to miners.  
      This will allow richer and more complex workloads beyond today's single-prompt tasks.  
    
    ### Rollout Plan
    - **Testnest first** → Live right now (uid 160)
    - **Mainnet 1 week later** → mandatory for all miners and validators.  
    
    ### 🚨 Action Required
    Please plan to **upgrade immediately once v2.18.53 is live**.  
    Without upgrading, your miner/validator will no longer function in Subnet 33.

**04:17 papercirer:** Validators generate the reference tags dynamically from the task they receive. These tags serve as the ground truth used to evaluate miners and calculate their scores. The validator’s role is precisely to establish that reference output and measure miner alignment against it.
    
    If the tags were pre-generated on the backend and distributed to validators, the evaluation would be equivalent, since they would be generated using the same method.
    Every validator task produces a self-consistent evaluation baseline. So even if another validator generated slightly different tags, miners are always scored relative to the same reference for that round, which keeps the process fair.
    
    Could you please clarify how your suggestion would improve the evaluation process?

**23:33 papercirer:** We've completed our initial investigation regarding the windows mentioned previously.
    
    These cases come from conversation transcriptions on our side. When those are later split into windows on the validators, a few fragments can capture small sections with transcription artifacts or hallucinations, which leads to meaningless snippets like the ones you've seen.
    
    That said, these represent a very small percentage of all windows sent to miners and a many conditions have to align for them to appear. It's obviously hard to generate meaningful tags from those, and we completely understand the frustration.
    
    We're already working on improvements to make sure this doesn't happen again:
    
    - Filtering -> we'll add a layer to automatically filter out these bad windows before they reach miners.
    - Task variety -> we'll increase the number of Common Crawl tasks to bring more diverse tagging content.
    - New task types -> we're preparing to send Ipsos tasks and other new types through the subnet soon.
    
    In the future, we also want to add even more visibility on the API side so we can publicly ensure the API isn't being used in unintended ways.
    
    Low-quality windows also hurt tagging quality on our end, so we're just as motivated to clean them up. Thanks for your patience and for flagging these edge cases. Your feedback helps us keep improving the subnet for everyone.
    
    Happy mining! ⛏️

**21:29 INTERN | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** As far as we know, this is an apples-to-oranges comparison. Alteryx (which now includes Trifacta), TIBCO Clarity, and OpenRefine are data cleaning and transformation platforms—they fix errors, remove duplicates, standardize formats, and reshape data that's already structured (like databases, spreadsheets, and tables).
    ReadyAI operates in a different space: we focus on data annotation and semantic tagging. We take unstructured data (raw podcast audio from RSS feeds, unstructured survey responses, social media content) and convert it into labeled, structured datasets with metadata. This creates AI-ready training data.
    From what we can tell, those data preparation tools don't perform annotation or labeling tasks—that's simply not what they're designed for. So there isn't really a direct cost comparison to make between ReadyAI and those platforms.
    However, when it comes to annotation tasks specifically, our published benchmark shows that ReadyAI's subnet miners achieved 0.96 annotation accuracy, outperforming GPT-4o (0.65) and Mechanical Turk workers (0.52), while reducing per-task cost by approximately 660× compared to MTurk's $0.12 per annotation task.
    Our enterprise customers use ReadyAI for tasks like coding open-ended survey responses, structuring large document collections for knowledge management systems, and building labeled training datasets—all centered on annotation rather than data cleaning or transformation.
    If your research is focused on annotation and labeling costs for AI training data, that's where ReadyAI excels. If you're looking at traditional ETL (extract, transform, load) and data cleaning workflows, those other tools serve that different purpose. Some enterprises might actually use both—ReadyAI to create labeled datasets from unstructured sources, then tools like Alteryx for downstream cleaning and transformation for specific analytics use cases.

**14:51 papercirer:** Hey Josh,
    
    For the dereg: it happens. This subnet is highly competitive, you have to compete against other miners that have been there for a while and had time to fine tune their techniques. You are immune for 24 hours and then if you are the miner with the least incentive when someone registers you get kicked out.
    
    For the testing: you should totally try on testnet and make sure your stuff works properly there before competing on the main net. What I suggest is that you either run a miner and a validator on test net to test the full loop quickly or you run a local chain and test everything yourself there for optimal testing loop speed.
    
    For bedrock: it's not supported out of the box on the base repo, you will have to do a custom implementation for it yourself.
    
    For your UID on WandB: you can DM me and I can double check, but it should've appeared.
    
    Incentive, emmission stake and trust numbers are enough to see if you miner will be deregistered, you can vizualise all the miners here: https://taostats.io/subnets/33/distribution
    Returning tags is not the only thing required to stay registered, you have to send better tags than others.
    
    Hope it helps 🙂

"It's the story that makes the most sense to me" is not evidence, though.

**13:58 Kat | Fren One:** No.  vTrust is a metric that reflect how much a *validator* is in consensus with the majority stake (it's a measure of how much a validator is trusted by the rest of the network: https://docs.learnbittensor.org/miners#inspecting-uids).
    
    "trust" (no "v") is the measure of how trusted a *miner* is, so that's a metric that you'd want to monitor.  However, I don't think there's going to be a way to reliably measure what you're getting on *testnet* for trust as opposed to what you'd get on *mainnet* -- mainnet is different (more validators, for one thing).
    
    On testnet, what you want to do is make sure that you're covering the basics: is the miner operating?  Is it communicating with the testnet validator? Is it receiving tasks, and mining tags, and is the validator on the other end receiving that submission?
    
    What I'd recommend you do is try to get a sense of how frequently the timeouts are occurring.  For example, if you go through your own logs and determine that yes, your average response time on testnet is 15 seconds, I would personally recommend that you work on improving that.  The timeout is 12 seconds. You don't want an *average* that's higher than that; it means you're probably missing too many opportunities to get your mined tags submitted, especially if you have not fine-tuned the base miner.  
    
    Mainnet is fiercely competitive; on mainnet, you should be *solely focused* on improving the *quality* of your miner's submissions there, and not having to worry about time (unless that time is being impacted by the fine-tuning you're doing).
    
    So, if your base miner's average response time on *testnet* is indeed 15 seconds, I'd recommend that you work on improving that before trying to make the move to mainnet.
**14:02 Kat | Fren One:** A couple of things to check out:
    
    o Ping the endpoint you're using from your server.  If there's an excessive ping time, try to figure out why.   But also check the ping to the *mainnet* endpoint you're using.  It might be significantly different than testnet (if it's faster, it could be an indicator that the problem won't be so bad when you move to mainnet).  If you're noticing really excessive ping times to both, work with your service provider to see if there's something in your server configurations that you can change, or if there's some kind of change they can make on their end.
    
    o If you're using the finney public endpoint, that could be a problem (*everyone* uses that). Consider spinning up a lite subtensor node to act as your own private endpoint into the network.  https://docs.learnbittensor.org/subtensor-nodes for the documentation on this, and testnet is an excellent place to practice with them.
**15:05 JoshMaking:** ok thank you so much. and where do i check my trust graph ?
**15:06 JoshMaking:** and whats a good value of trust ? 
    again , the timeout occurs so rarely , and when it doesnt my response is less than 5 sec
**15:20 Kat | Fren One:** Right, but what is the ratio of timeouts to successful responses?  If every other query from a validator results in a timeout, that's 50%, which is not great.  If it's only once in a while, it's probably okay, but I'd still recommend taking a look at it to make sure it's not something you can control (if it is, you should consider controlling it).  Remember that later, when you start fine-tuning your model for quality, it might slow down your model's responses.  So giving yourself some room to breathe in is, imo, a good idea.
    
    As for `trust`, I couldn't say.  Probably the best thing to do is look at the metagraph for subnet 33 on Taostats, and then sort by incentive (those are the rewards that miners receive).  Look at the top miners (the ones receiving the most incentive) and then look at their `trust` (which should be part of the metagraph).  
    
    But I think that `trust` is really not all that important.  <@188485281148698624> , <@165159758167277568> , I'm pretty sure that most subnets don't actually use it (the scoring, which determines how your miner is weighted, is what's primarily important) -- that's the case for ReadyAI, correct?
    
    (So, in short, if you look at the top miners' `trust` and don't see any real correlation between trust and their incentives, that's why, and don't worry about it.)  
    
    I'd recommend focusing on the scoring in the wandb tables, not the trust metric in the metagraph (unless papiercirer or ThePianoGuy say otherwise).
**15:32 papercirer:** Yeah the trust is the consensus calculated by validators. If your score is closer to other miners it means a higher trust. Just like vTrust and weights but for miners. That being said, you should focus on the incentives of your miner.
    
    You can see their value over time using this tool: https://grafana.bactensor.io/d/miner/metagraph-miner?orgId=1&var-subnet=33
    
    We're happy to help when we can! Just a reminder that most common questions are already documented here in the channel or somewhre else in the main BT Discord, so it’s best to look there first. It keeps things efficient for everyone.

**18:25 ThePianoGuy:** # 🚀 Upcoming Validator & Miner Release – LlmLib Rework & Cost Reduction – v2.21.56
    
    Hello everyone! <@&1237015679023059017>
    
    A new release is coming <t:1764874800:f>, introducing a complete rework of the LLM Library and significant cost reductions for validators.
    
    ⚠️ **This upgrade is required for validators and recommended for miners.**
    
    **PR:** https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/98
    
    ## ✨ Key Highlights
    This release focuses on streamlining the codebase by removing legacy support and refactoring the `LlmLib`. For validators, this includes a configuration change that lowers operating costs without sacrificing accuracy. We are also testing how new models could be leveraged to improve the quality of the tasks and of the scoring for miners.
    
    ## ⛏️ What It Means for Miners
    - **No change to scoring algorithm or prompts**: The change only impacts the conversation quality check that is done on the validator side.
    - **Existing miners will continue to work**: If miners don't update, their miners will continue to work "as-is". The upgrade is still recommended to limit code drift.
    - **Changes to `llmLib` initialization**: Miners must now use the provided factory function `get_llm_backend()`. (Refer to `conversationgenome/task/ConversationTaggingTask.py` for an example).
    - **Legacy Removal:** Miners relying on the deprecated legacy mechanism will no longer work on the subnet.
    
    ## 🧩 What It Means for Validators
    - 💵 **Lower Operating Costs:** The default model for conversation quality validation has switched from `gpt-4o` to `gpt4.1-mini`. For now all other prompts remain exactly as they were.
    - **Streamlined Logic:** Legacy support for the old `forward` method is removed. Validators will no longer retry on deprecated pathways when a miner returns a 5xx error; these will now only be logged.
    
    ## 🚦 Rollout Plan
    Testnet: Live now for initial testing
    Mainnet: Scheduled for rollout <t:1764874800:f>
    
    Happy validating and mining ⛏️

    <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    We have been one of the longest running subnets with 100% miner emissions on. With the new Tao Flow system, we do not believe this is sustainable. We will be activating the burn (we are the 89th subnet to do so) because it allows us to create a more stable Alpha, reduce sell pressure, and protect long-term holders while we get emissions flowing again.
    
    We will be burning 90% of the mining emissions to start and we will continue to evaluate the right burn in light of emissions and revenue generation.
    
    ⚠️ **This upgrade is required for validators**  
    Please plan to upgrade immediately once the new version is live.
    
    **PR:** https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/99
    
    ### What it means for miners:
    - Lower short-term rewards, yes
        - But Subnet33 remains one of the lowest-cost subnets, so miners will still be profitable even with the burn active
    - More stable Alpha because supply pressure drops
    - Stronger long-term rewards once emissions return
    If registration costs become too big a barrier because of the burn, we’ll try to step in to keep things manageable.
    
    ### What it means for Alpha:
    Burning reduces supply and stabilizes the subnet
    It's a clear signal that we are actively steering Subnet-33 to protect the ecosystem and long-term sustainability.
    
    ### What's coming next:
    - 🏡 New partnership in the real-estate data space
    - 🧠 New tasks tied to that domain
    
    This is a major step forward for Subnet33 and positions us for an even bigger Q1.
    Subnet33 is just getting warmed up. ⛏️

**00:34 papercirer:** # 🚀 Upcoming Validator & Miner Release – Named Entity Recognition (NER) Task – v2.23.58
    <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    Hello everyone!
    
    A new release is coming <t:1766088000:f>, introducing a major new task type: Named Entity Recognition (NER).
    
    ⚠️ This upgrade is required for validators and miners.
    PR: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/101
    
    ## ✨ Key Highlights
    We are launching Named Entity Recognition (NER) as our next task type, enabling the full universe of structured data functionality on the subnet. This release launches with a real estate-focused use case: Regulatory Radar.
    
    This feature processes regulatory information, such as city council meetings, zoning decisions and permit approvals to extract entities and signals that move real estate markets. This is part of our AcquiOS platform, with enterprise customers **Gelt Venture Partners** and **Archer Equities** already onboard.
    
    ## ⛏️ What It Means for Miners
    - **New Task Type**: Miners will now receive a fourth task type: `named_entities_extraction`.
    - **Objective**: The goal of the new task is to parse unstructured text and generate tags corresponding to named entities.
    - **Target Categories**: Miners must focus on people, organizations, locations, laws/statutes, budgets and specific projects
    - **Scoring Mechanism**: For this initial release, the task will use the existing mechanism to ensure a smooth rollout.
    
    ## 🧩 What It Means for Validators
    - **New Validation Logic**: Validators will now generate NER tasks
    - **New requirements**: This release adds a new dependency for validators, make sure to update using `requirements.txt`
    - **Web connection**: The validators will need to fetch data on the web to generate the new task type, make sure your validator is setup to allow outgoing calls
    
    ## 🚦 Rollout Plan
    **Testnet**: Live now for testing  
    **Mainnet**: Scheduled rollout <t:1766088000:f>
    
    Happy validating and mining ⛏️

**23:28 davfields | ReadyAI [τ,ט]:** **Technical Paper: Non-Deterministic Enrichment Tasks**
    
    We've spent the last few weeks rearchitecting how SN33 handles miner tasks. Sharing the technical details now—launch is week of 1/19.
    
    **The problem:**
    Most subnet tasks are deterministic. Input X → Output Y. Works for inference and compute, but constrains dataset generation. There's no single "correct" way to enrich a source document—and in a decentralized, adversarial environment, verifying proof-of-work on limited datasets is hard when outputs must be identical.
    
    **What we built:**
    A task primitive where the same input produces different valid outputs depending on configurable parameters.
    
    Source document → persona-driven inference → contextual search queries → structured enrichment output
    
    Same transcript through an "Opportunistic Investor" lens → queries about rezoning and distressed assets.
    Same transcript through a "Real Estate Lender" lens → queries about refinancing risk and sponsor strength.
    
    Both valid. Both useful. Infinitely scalable.
    
    **Scaling math:**
    - 1 source doc × 20 personas × 10 queries × 10 results = 2,000 enrichment data points
    - 1,000 source docs = 2,000,000 data points
    - Add personas → output multiplies without changing source material
    
    **What's next:**
    - Launch next week (1/19) serving RE customers with 20 deployed personas
    - Expanding to llms.txt enrichment for training data synthesis
    - Cross-subnet integration 
    
    Full technical paper on X:
    
    https://x.com/DavFields/status/2011218089439084661?s=20
    (embed) New from SN33: Non\-Deterministic Enrichment Tasks  
    
    We solved a structural problem in subnet design: how to generate infinite valid outputs from finite inputs while maintaining verifiable quality\.  
    
    Same source doc \+ different persona = different valid queries\. Infinitely

    ## ✨ Key Highlights
    We are accelerating innovation while ensuring stability. This release introduces a modular Extension System, allowing miners to layer logic, prompts, and optimizations on top of the core codebase without direct modification.

    - ** Safe Experimentation**: Extensions provide a sandbox to test new prompts, models, and response styles without touching core SN33 code.

**13:49 papercirer:** # 🚀 Upcoming Validator & Miner Release – Non-Deterministic Data Enrichment – v2.25.60 <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    Hello everyone!  
    We are evolving SN33 with a new task primitive: Non-Deterministic Enrichment (NER).
    
    ⚠️ This upgrade is required for validators and miners.
    
    This type of task won't be sent on mainnet until next week to allow time for updates!
    
    PR: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/106
    
    ## ✨ Key Highlights
    We are evolving SN33 beyond simple inputs and outputs. This release introduces Persona-Driven Synthesis, allowing the network to generate infinite, high-value datasets from finite source material.
    
    By processing documents through 20+ specific "Personas" (e.g., Opportunistic Investors, ESG Specialists), we can now explode a single document into thousands of unique, context-aware data points. This initial launch targets the Real Estate Domain, enriching publicly available data from multiple cities.
    
    ## 🌐 What It Means for the Subnet
    - Infinite Scalability: We have unlocked the ability to exponentially multiply our data output.
    - High-Value Datasets: This approach generates proprietary, multi-perspective data that is highly valuable for real-world applications like AcquiOS.
    - Future Expansion: While launching in Real Estate, this paves the way for expansion into llms.txt generation and M&A data synthesis, significantly broadening the subnet's addressable market.
    
    ## ⛏️ What It Means for Miners
    - Persona-Driven Inference: You will now receive tasks requiring you to use higher-order logic to generate and aggregate supplementary research data.
    
    ## 🧩 What It Means for Validators
    - Quality-Within-Constraints: Validators will now verify miner outputs not just for factual accuracy, but for thematic relevance and persona consistency.
    
    ## 🚦 Rollout Plan
    Testnet: Live now  
    Mainnet: Scheduled for <t:1769180400:f>
    
    Happy validating and mining ⛏️

    SN33 has transitioned from static infrastructure to a fully elastic, containerized execution layer that scales dynamically with demand.

    All validators need to update quickly to avoid having their *VTrust* impacted by this model change and risk having their rewards impacted.

    In preparation for the phase-out of OpenAI's ⁨`gpt-4o`⁩ model, we are updating the default configurations to the latest supported alternatives.
    
    From our testing it delivers **lower token costs** and **dramatically improved output quality**, directly improving the bottom line for network participants and the quality of the data we are generating.
    
    ### ⚠️ Important Configuration Check
    **If your ⁨`.env`⁩ file contains an ⁨`OPENAI_MODEL`⁩ override, this update will NOT apply automatically.**
    
    You must review your configuration. If you have hardcoded a specific model version, you risk using a deprecated model. In doubt, we recommend removing the ⁨`OPENAI_MODEL`⁩ override to inherit the new defaults.
    
    ### 🌐 What It Means for the Network
    - **Lower OpEx:** The new default models are more efficient, meaning your daily operating costs will decrease while maintaining or improving score performance.
    - **Reliability:** Migrating now prevents potential outages or instability associated with deprecated endpoints.
    - **Future-Proofing:** Removes technical debt and ensures the subnet remains aligned with the latest industry standards.

    ## What We're Building
    
    The web is searchable, but it isn't organized. SN33 is changing that.
    
    We take Common Crawl pages and produce structured metadata that language models, agents, and retrieval systems can consume immediately - queryable, consistent, and formatted to the emerging llms.txt standard. With this release, we're enriching entire web sites, not just individual pages - positioning SN33 to become the largest producer of llms.txt files in the world.

    ## What's New in v2
    
    Persona-Driven Enrichment. Instead of a single flat extraction per page, the system now uses LLMs and persona-based web searches to generate deep, multi-perspective context around each target webpage.
    
    Each page gets processed through multiple analytical personas (Tech Analyst, Policy Reviewer, Cultural Historian, etc.), producing structured metadata that captures multiple valid interpretations of the same content. We're appending layers of semantic intelligence to the world's largest open web archive.
    
    ### For Miners
    
    Enriched inputs - you'll now receive webpage content alongside persona-driven enrichment bundles with multi-perspective context data. Your task: synthesize these enriched inputs into high-fidelity structured metadata.

    New scoring surface against enriched inputs and updated output structure. Upgrade required

    ## ✨ Key Highlights
    
    We are refining the subnet based on performance and data quality metrics. Our analysis shows that processing "Enriched Snippets" yields higher quality data that processing full websites as enrichment.
    
    This release also standardizes our enrichment logic across task types. We are shifting the NER task to focus on titles and snippets rather than full webpage content.
    
    ### ⛏️ What It Means for Miners
    - High-Signal Inputs: You will no longer receive full website bodies for enrichment in NER tasks. Enrichment data is now streamlined to title and snippet.
    - Efficiency: Reduced data transfer means faster processing times and lower bandwidth requirements.
    
    ### 🧩 What It Means for Validators
    - Reduced Overhead: Validating snippets instead of full DOM trees significantly lowers the compute and network cost per validation.
    - Removed External Dependencies: This update removes the requirement to fetch external webpages during validation. This ensures significantly higher reliability by eliminating potential network timeouts, IP blocks and scraping failures.
    
    ### 🌐 What It Means for the Network
    - Data Density: By filtering out the noise of full HTML structure, we are generating a cleaner, more actionable knowledge graph.
    - Metric-Driven Optimization: This shift is a direct result of evaluating Value per Compute Unit. We are producing the same high-quality intelligence with a fraction of the overhead.
    
    ### 🚦 Rollout Plan
    
    Testnet: Live now for initial testing
    Mainnet: Scheduled for rollout <t:1772478000:f>

**12:31 papercirer:** Hey, thanks for flagging this, it's always good when miners are paying attention to scoring patterns!
    
    That said, I'd ask that we hold off on conclusions like self-mining or running custom code without something concrete to back it up. Those are strong claims, and jumping to them without evidence isn't fair to anyone.
    
    What you're seeing is most likely just normal subnet behavior:
    
    - Different validators pull different conversations and generate their own independent ground truth: since scoring is based on cosine distance between your tags and that ground truth, the difficulty of the task directly affects your score. A lower score on one validator doesn't mean something shady is going on, it may just mean the task was harder.
    - We deliberately add non-determinism through prompt enrichment:  this is a core anti-gaming mechanism. It means even similar-looking tasks can differ under the hood.
    
    The scoring logic is also identical across all validators and fully open source. You can read it, audit it and run it yourself. The best way to see if you are competitive is to compare your score vs. other miners facing the same challenge.
    
    Honestly, it cannot be more transparent than this. WandB runs are fully public. You can see the exact git commit running on each validator, the full logs, and scores over time for every run. If something was off, it would be visible to the entire community. There is nowhere to hide anything.
    
    Take a look at the owner validator's WandB runs. Is your miner competitive with others when receiving the same challenge? That's the question that matters.
    
    Take a look and let us know what you find: https://wandb.ai/afterparty/conversationgenome

**21:18 papercirer:** Fair enough, let me give you some context on how the scoring actually works:
    
    Score differences between validators are expected. Each validator independently generates its own ground-truth tags via LLM. There is no shared seed or shared temperature. It selects different random conversation windows and queries a different random subset of miners each round. Essentially, every validator is grading against its own answer key. These differences also compound over time through EMA weight accumulation. 
    
    What actually matters is your aggregate weight across all validators, not your score from any single one at a given moment.
    
    Also worth noting: your EMA evolves continuously. A streak of lower scores will temporarily pull your weight down, but it recovers as your scores come back up. It can do the same on the other side too!
    
    One more factor that contributes to variance: when miners have the same score, their positions in the weight distribution are randomly shuffled. Weight is then assigned based on rank position via a cubic distribution and not score value directly. So two miners with identical scores can end up with different weights depending purely on where they land in the shuffle. This is another reason why point-in-time comparisons between validators can look inconsistent even when everything is working correctly.
**21:23 papercirer:** Also! I you'd like to check, wandb shows final miner scores over time across all validators. You'll see that the aggregate is pretty consistent and the average stays in the same range regardless of individual validator variance. 
    
    You could also dig into your scores broken down by task type (that's not on WandB though) it's possible your miner performs better on certain task types and happened to get a heavier concentration of those on one validator vs another. That said, over multiple days, it should average out to roughly the same place across all validators.
    
    The WandB is here: https://wandb.ai/afterparty/conversationgenome

**00:38 papercirer:** This usually means your miner got deregistered. If the hot and cold keys for UID 191 changed it pretty much confirms it
**00:45 papercirer:** The registration and deregistration cycle is handled by the chain itself, not the subnet code
**01:24 Faad:** Why though it got deregistered? I was getting tasks consistently and successfully completed those and my alpha points were increasing and all of a sudden this happened.
**01:27 Faad:** So what could be this issue then? I lost my time, registration fee, run pod subscription and gpt tokens (even though it’s small amount but it’s frustrating when your effort go in vein)
**01:34 papercirer:** Getting deregistered is frustrating. Losing registration fees and compute costs stings, especially when you felt like things were working. That's the reality of Bittensor though, you will have to get accustomed to it 😛
    
    Here's what happened: the subnet runs on a competitive registration model. Every time a new miner registers, the miner with the lowest emission weight that isn't immune gets bumped out to make room. It's not necessarily about doing anything wrong. It just means other miners on the subnet were outscoring you at that point in time.
    
    Alpha increasing is a good sign, but what matters for survival is your score relative to everyone else. If the overall competition level rises (more miners, better miners), the floor rises with it. Getting alpha and staying registered is not really tied. You'll get more if your score is higher, but that's it.
    
    The path forward is to iterate on your miner. Optimize your scoring, look at what the top miners might be doing differently and come back stronger. It's a grind, but that's the nature of the game on Bittensor. You've already got the basics running which puts you ahead of most people starting out. 
    
    Keep it up ⛏️
**01:38 papercirer:** Also, when you register, you have 24 hours of immunity. After that, if you are the miner with the lowest score, you'll likely get bumped

**15:45 papercirer:** # 🚀 llms.txt dataset MCP - your coding agent just got a lot smarter
    <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    Coding agents hallucinate APIs. They scrape noisy HTML. They reason from stale training data. We built something to fix that.
    
    The **llms.txt Reference MCP** gives any coding agent instant, structured access to **10,000+ domains** from the SN33 dataset.
    
    https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/tree/main/llms_txt_reference_mcp
    
    ## Available tools
    
    - `search_sites(query)` — full-text search across 10K+ llms.txt files
    - `get_site(domain)` — fetch structured docs for a specific domain
    - `lookup_domain(url)` — resolve any URL to its llms.txt entry
    - `list_sites(tld?)` — browse all indexed domains, optionally by TLD
    
    ## Works with OpenClaw & Claude Code
    
    Drop it into **OpenClaw** or **Claude Code**: add the MCP server to your config and your agent immediately has grounded access to 10K+ real API docs — no extra setup, no plugins, no scraping.
    
    ## Benchmarks incoming
    
    We're currently running head-to-head comparisons between vanilla models and MCP-equipped models on real coding tasks. Early results are promising: fewer hallucinations, more grounded reasoning, better code. We'll share the full benchmarks soon.
    
    ## Beyond coding agents
    
    The same benefits apply anywhere an agent needs to understand the web — a research agent surveying a topic, a sales tool qualifying a prospect, a content agent understanding a site's focus before drafting. Anywhere an LLM guesses at what a website is or does, this MCP gives it a grounded answer instantly.
    
    ## 10K domains is just the start
    
    📍 Roadmap: 10K → 100K → 1M — continuously updated as SN33 processes new Common Crawl releases. **Browse the dataset now on our new website**: https://readyai.ai/ — request feature coming soon.

**21:02 ThePianoGuy:** # 📊 Benchmarks are in — llms.txt MCP improves coding agents
    
    Hi everyone! <@&1237015679023059017> 
    
    We ran **OpenAI GPT-5.4-nano** head-to-head on **GitChameleon**, a benchmark built to punish hallucinated APIs and stale training data.
    Vanilla model vs. the same model wired up to the **llms.txt Reference MCP**.
    
    These are early results - more runs and deeper analysis are coming soon!
    
    ## 📈 The numbers
    Across our benchmarking runs:
    * **Vanilla model:** 40.9% pass rate
    * **With llms.txt MCP:** 44.8% pass rate
    * **Delta: +3.9 percentage points (~+9.5% relative lift)**
    
    Grounded lookups are already outperforming pure parametric guessing.
    This isn't a massive leap yet — but for lightweight, doc-level grounding, it's a meaningful and consistent lift.
    
    ## 🚀 Powered by SN33
    The MCP is the delivery mechanism — the actual grounding signal comes from the subnet.
    Every domain SN33 processes is another API your agent stops hallucinating.
    
    ## 🏗️ This is the floor, not the ceiling
    A few honest observations from the run:
    * `llms.txt` is a **map of a site's docs**, not a structured, function-level API reference.
    * The benchmark is brutal by design — version-pinned, narrow tasks where even tiny API drift causes failure.
    * The current lift comes from relatively shallow document grounding.
    
    The path to larger gains is clear:
    * More domains
    * Richer per-domain extraction
    * Structured API-level grounding instead of high-level doc maps
    * More targeted and specific mining tasks
    
    ## ℹ️ More info
    Browse the dataset: https://readyai.ai/
    Wire up the MCP: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/tree/main/llms_txt_reference_mcp
    Use our benchmark script: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/120
    Learn more about GitChameleon: https://gitchameleon-2-0.github.io/
    
    Let's keep building ⛏️

**08:03 Dreander:** I looked through that repository, and under the current conditions it seems overengineered - at least until miner emissions are restored, since it would require significantly higher AWS spending.
    
    Here is what I propose instead:
    
    Right now, validators send requests to the database to receive tasks, signing those requests with their keys.
    
    We could implement a similar handler for miners. Miners would send a request like: “miner served here: 1.2.3.4:5678”, signing it with their key in the same way. This signature would also be verified on the ReadyAI side.
    
    Then, every N minutes - for example, once per hour - validators would query ReadyAI and request the current list of miner endpoints: [(IP, port), ...], 256 entries in total. Validators would use that list instead of relying on the metagraph data.
    
    As a result, the metagraph would no longer expose any IP addresses related to miners, and attackers would no longer be able to target them directly.

**20:41 Kat | Fren One:** The ideal subnet mechanism (that's providing a sellable product), imo, is this:
    Participant income based on (for miners) quality -> quality output -> valuable service -> more customers -> participant income... 
    
    In other words, something of a flywheel.
    
    I think that setting up a process where by revenue goes directly into income (via the underlying swap pool) is a good step.  DDoS protection is another, because it helps to prevent one person or group from hogging the subnet, which is bad because a) lack of competition and therefore real growth and development and b) it's brittle to have a limited number of people providing your service.  What if they decide it's no longer worth their trouble and decamp all at once?  Sure, you might be able to attract more miners, but there's going to be a gap. **23:03 papercirer:** # 🚀 SN33 ReadyAI - Encrypted Endpoint Commitments (Anti-DDoS) Release Dropping Tomorrow
      
    This release ships a major networking change: miner IPs are no longer exposed in the metagraph. Endpoints are now encrypted on-chain and only decryptable by validators holding the subnet private key.
    
    We will be released tomorrow <t:1779976800:f>
    
    ## 🔒 What's new
    - Encrypted endpoint commitments: Miners publish their ip:port (and hotkey) as a NaCl sealed-box ciphertext to the `Commitments`  pallet. Validators read the whole subnet's commitments in one `query_map` call and decrypt locally.
     - Replay/copy protection:Hotkey is embedded in the commitment payload, so a miner can't reuse another miner's commitment.
    
    ##  ⚠️  Action required
    
    - Validators: You must set the decryption key in your environment variables before starting: `COMMITMENT_PRIVATE_KEY=<key>`
      - Testnet key is in `env.example`.
      - Mainnet key will be distributed securely to validators.
    - Miners:  Pull the latest code and restart. Your miner will publish its encrypted commitment automatically on startup; no manual key handling required.
    
    Full details here in the [PR](https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/122)
    Questions / issues -> ping us here 🙏
    
    <@&1237015679023059017>

**13:42 papercirer:** The thing to keep in mind is that established miners are sitting at a fully ramped EMA, while every new miner starts from zero. 24h is good average spot for what it takes for a legit new miner to build enough EMA to actually compete. If we cut that down, we'll be impacting good miners before their score catches up to their real output, forcing them to re-register and pay again, which raises the entry barrier.
    
    That's not just unfair to individuals, it's bad for the subnet. If every new registration starts with a handicap steep enough that they're likely to get dereg'd before they can prove themselves, people stop bothering to compete. You end up with a full metagraph and no incoming pressure to improve. That kills innovation. The temporary lower-quality scores we might get from immune miners are a much smaller cost than choking off the pipeline of new talent

    Conversation submission is now available through our Jobs API! You can submit conversations directly for processing on the network. Read the docs here https://api.readyai.ai/jobs-api/docs

    **Consistent Enrichment**: Conversations join NER and Websites under one unified enrichment primitive.

    **Open Submission**: The Jobs API opens the door for external conversation data to flow into the subnet.  
    
    ### ⛏️ What It Means for Miners
    **Enriched Inputs**: Tasks now include enrichment context alongside the conversation window. You'll derive tags from both and aggregate them into a combined result. **Important**: You will need to update your miner's conversation-tagging code.
    
    ### 🧩 What It Means for Validators
    **Combined Ground Truth**: Validators build ground-truth metadata from the conversation plus enrichment, scoring miners on thematic relevance across both sources.
    
    ## 🚦 Rollout Plan
    Testnet: Live now
    Mainnet: Scheduled for <t:1781632810:f>

**22:34 ThePianoGuy:** # 🚀 Jobs API Update – Priority Tiers
    
    Hello everyone! <@&1237015679023059017> 
    You can now choose **how fast you want your jobs handled**. The Jobs API supports priority tiers, letting you trade cost against turnaround on a per-job basis.
    
    ## ✨ Key Highlights
    Both the quote and job submission endpoints accept an optional `priority` field. Pick a tier and the price scales off the normal rate — higher priority for time-sensitive work, lower priority to save when you're not in a rush.
    
    ## 📥 How to Use It
    Add `"priority": "HIGH"` (or `LOW` / `NORMAL` / `X_HIGH`) to your quote and job requests. The same value must be sent on both — a mismatch is rejected. The default is `NORMAL`, so leave it out entirely and jobs behave exactly as before.
    Read the docs here https://api.readyai.ai/jobs-api/docs
    
    ### 🌐 What It Means for You
    **Flexible Throughput**: Match each job's cost to how quickly you need it back.
    **Predictable Pricing**: A simple multiplier on the rate you already know — quoted up front.
    **Zero Migration**: Existing integrations keep working untouched; `priority` defaults to `NORMAL`.
    
    ## 🚦 Rollout Plan
    Mainnet: Live now!
    
    Happy building 🛠️

**21:11 ThePianoGuy:** # 🚀 Jobs API Update – Extra Tags
    
    Hello everyone! <@&1237015679023059017> 
    Today we're releasing a widely requested feature for  **richer tag coverage** on a per-job basis. The Jobs API now supports an optional `extraTags` flag that has your job processed by more miners before the result is finalized.
    
    ## ✨ Key Highlights
    Both the quote and job submission endpoints accept an optional `extraTags` boolean. When set, the aggregator waits for more miner results before completing the job — broader, deeper metadata for the jobs that need it. This multiplies the price by **1.5×**, and stacks on top of priority (e.g. `X_HIGH` + `extraTags` = 2.0 × 1.5 = 3.0×).
    
    ## 📥 How to Use It
    Add `"extraTags": true` to your quote and job requests. The same value must be sent on both — a mismatch is rejected. The default is `false`.
    Read the docs here https://api.readyai.ai/jobs-api/docs
    
    ### 🌐 What It Means for You
    **Richer Datasets**: More miners contribute, so completed jobs carry broader, higher-confidence tags.
    **Higher Metadata Confidence**: Deeper consensus on important jobs reduces ambiguity and improves downstream AI performance.
    **Capture More Long-Tail Signals**: Surface tags that a smaller pass might miss — better coverage for niche or specialized content.
    **Stronger Training Data**: More comprehensive labels mean better accuracy when the output feeds model training.
    
    ## 🚦 Rollout Plan
    Mainnet: Live now!
    
    Happy building 🛠️

**13:31 papercirer:** Thanks for flagging. This is an error we see occasionally, usually for one of two reasons:
    
    1. An issue with the embedding/LLM provider like transient API error, rate-limiting, an expired/invalid key, or the provider returning malformed or inconsistently-sized embeddings. When that happens the similarity calculation fails and the score is set to zero.
    2.Tags that couldn't be cleanly processed. In rare cases a miner's tags don't survive validation/embedding, which can also zero out a score.
    
    The intermittent, come-and-go nature of these errors points to the provider side as the more likely cause. We'll keep monitoring, and we're adding more detailed logging around the failure so we can confirm the exact trigger next time it appears.

**23:26 papercirer:** The latest update deprecated the use of our current bittensor package version. I'll be pushing an update shortly and everyone should upgrade!
**23:36 papercirer:** # Subnet 33 - Required Update: update to bittensor 10.3.0
    
    We've upgraded the codebase from bittensor 9 → 10.3.0. bittensor 10 renamed/removed several APIs, which broke the on-chain commitment system (how validators discover miner endpoints). All miners and validators must update.
    
    ⚠️ Action required (both miners & validators):
    ```
    git pull
    pip install -r requirements.txt        # pulls bittensor==10.3.0
    # restart your neuron (pm2 restart / systemctl restart, etc.)
    ```
    
    ▎ If you upgrade in place and hit a scalecodec / cyscale conflict on startup, run:
    ▎ pip uninstall scalecodec cyscale -y && pip install cyscale --force-reinstall
    
    ### What was fixed (commitment layer):
    - get_metadata removed in bt10 → validator endpoint refresh restored
    - publish_metadata renamed → miners can publish their endpoint again
    - Commitment decode format changed in bt10 → validators were silently dropping every commitment (Commitments: 0 total); now resolving correctly
    
    ### How to verify after updating:
    - Validators: logs should show using committed endpoints
    - Miners: check your process is up and reachable on your served IP:port
    
    Please update at your earliest convenience 🙏 
    If you have questions drop them here!
    
    PR is here: https://github.com/afterpartyai/bittensor-conversation-genome-project/pull/133
    
    <@&1237015679023059017>

**11:03 αWolf [ τ, τ ]:** You are right that I should be precise, so I checked the validator code again.
    
    TaskBundleLib.get_task_bundle() reserves the bundle and then calls task_bundle.setup(), where the validator generates the metadata. For conversation enrichment, the validator randomly selects enrichment search results, generates tags from them, and combines those tags with the full-conversation tags. The selected enrichment text is also included in enrichment_lines sent to miners, so I am not claiming that the enrichment content itself is hidden.
    
    However, the validator then calls:
    
    await vl.put_task(
        data=task_bundle.input.metadata.model_dump(),
    )
    
    before entering the loop that sends the masked tasks to miners. put_task() forwards that metadata to the configured ReadyAI write API, whose default host is db.conversations.xyz.
    
    Therefore, my statement came from the execution order in the public code. A more precise wording would be: the generated GT metadata is submitted to the ReadyAI write API before miner dispatch.
    
    I am not claiming this proves a leak or a server compromise. My point is only that, if unauthorized real-time read access existed, the final GT tags and vectors—not merely the enrichment text—could theoretically be exposed before miners respond. Whether that endpoint is securely protected is a separate question that cannot be answered from the public validator code alone.

**18:54 papercirer:** Hey everyone, I've read through the whole thread carefully. Thanks to those who took the time to actually go into the validator flow rather than just asserting things.
    
    First, one clarification, because a lot of the thread rests on it: running multiple hotkeys or coldkeys is not against the rules on SN33. It never has been. Registering more keys costs more and every key is scored independently on the work it submits. There's no bonus for volume. A miner with 180 keys and a good solution earns what those 180 keys score, the same as a miner with one key. So the key count on its own isn't evidence of anything. The question worth asking is whether the scoring is fair and that's what the points below are about.
    
    For the Dashboard: This has been on our roadmap and it slipped as we prioritized other features. I will see if we can give it increased priority and I'll share something concrete with the community as soon as I have a timeline.
    
    On reproducing the scores: a single conversation is used to generate multiple challenges, not one. Publishing the conversation, the GT and miner tags while it's still in rotation would provide a slight unfair-information problem although the enrichment process makes this a very slight advantages. As we have done in the past, we can release bundles of retired conversations (please see our Hugging Face dataset that has over 5000 conversations). If a new data conversation dataset dump is a priority for the community, please let us know.
    
    We don't currently persist the score attributed to each individual tag for a specific challenge. As we expand the types of tasks and add a new non-tag scoring mechanism, we will be expanding the metadata stored with each result and we'll put this on the list.
    
    More soon.
**19:48 Dreander:** Hi! Thank you very much for your response!
    
    The specific concern was that someone might have real-time access to the database and therefore know the validators’ correct answers before the validators begin scoring the miners.
    
    A dashboard would address this concern. However, while we’re waiting for that feature, I’d like to suggest a simple interim solution: could you change the order of operations so that the validator scores the miners first and only then sends its “correct” tags to the database? That way, any hypothetical bad actors would no longer have an advantage.
    
    More precisely, they would only have an advantage if they managed to compromise every validator on the subnet, which seems even more far-fetched.
    
    What do you think?
**19:56 papercirer:** Yes the `put_task` call currently happens before the masked tasks are dispatched to miners. There's no read exposure there, but the execution order could invite exactly the interpretation raised above and there's no reason for it to be ordered that way. We'll move it after miner dispatch.
**20:07 Dreander:** Thank you very much! I’m confident this will make a real difference.
    
    A special thank-you to <@1493533481337360516>  for identifying this issue and making such a valuable contribution to Subnet 33.
    
    Thanks to this change, we’ll be able to say with complete confidence that even the subnet organizers **cannot be accused of mining with privileged information, since they won’t have access to the correct answers before scoring takes place.**
    
    Thank you! 🤝
